content.text: I want to build a website using pathland that promotes it and also delivers a documentaion for it. For the documentation sites I would prefer to to be able to describe it using markdown. Not markdown via text views, as we need support for more markdown (images, table etc.). What do you think we lack to be able to build such a website?

# pathland-markdown — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **shared inline Markdown parser**: `no_std` + `alloc`, used by the Rust DSL directly and by foreign hosts through `pathland-markdown-capi`. It produces a `pathland_core::AttributedString` (style runs + links), not a separate AST. ## Implemented - Inline subset: `**bold**` / `__bold__` → `FONT_WEIGHT` 700, `*italic*` / `_italic_` → `FONT_STYLE` Italic, `` `code` `` → `FONT_DESIGN` Monospaced, `~~strikethrough~~` → `STRIKETHROUGH`, `[label](url)` → link run (label parsed recursively), and backslash escapes. - Nested emphasis with run splitting (`***`/`___` close italic then bold); intraword underscores stay literal (`snake_case`). - UTF-8 byte offsets in the produced runs; code spans do not parse inner markup. - Unit tests for markers, nesting, links, code, escapes, underscores, unmatched markers, and UTF-8 offsets. - Used by the Rust DSL: `pathland-engine` auto-parses `Node::markdown_text`. The Kotlin `Text(...)` path uses a **pure-Java behavioural port** in `pathland-view-core` (no native library); `pathland-markdown-capi` remains for non-JVM hosts. ## Not implemented / gaps - Block Markdown (headings, lists, paragraphs), reference links, images, and tables. --- # pathland-render-html (Rust) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming** pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once, and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`. > **JVM note:** the Spring Boot / Quarkus paths no longer load this crate through > JNA. `lib/java/pathland-render-html` is a **pure-Java behavioural port**, and > `GoldenConformanceTest` keeps it byte-identical to this canonical renderer. > The Rust crate remains the cross-language (C ABI) implementation and the > source of the committed golden fixtures. ## Implemented - **Window metadata → head**: `TITLE` → ``, `DESCRIPTION` → `<meta name="description">`, `LOCALE` → `<html lang>` (default `en`/`Pathland`); values escaped. Also: generic `LABEL` → `aria-label` (icon buttons), slider names on the inner input, `aria-hidden` on the non-visual media shell. - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta` is a per-render host option (`render_document_with_meta` / `render_document_linked_with_meta`) for the canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and JSON-LD. Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` still win; `DocumentMeta` title/description are fallbacks. JSON-LD derives a `WebPage` plus one `Article` per `ROLE_ARTICLE` (headline from the first heading, description from the first paragraph, image from the first `IMAGE`); `<`/`>`/`&` are unicode-escaped so app text cannot break out of the script element. `pathland_html_render_with_meta` exposes the same option over the C ABI (`PathlandHtmlMeta`). The canonical Rust output is pinned by `document_meta.document.html` and the Java port reproduces it byte-for-byte. - **`PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E)**: renders as a plain container box (a flex column, like a stack with one child) and lays out the (id-remapped) origin subtree the proxying server spliced in — the renderer holds no notion of "remote" (spec/PROXY.md §5). Without this arm the component fell to the `_ => String::new()` default and the spliced subtree was dropped. Covered by a unit test. - **Attributed text**: `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` decodes the binary payload into the node model and renders non-overlapping `<span style>` runs plus `<a href>` links (v1 attributes: font size/weight/color/style/design/underline/ strikethrough); text and URLs are escaped, and the plain text remains the fallback. Covered by a unit test. - **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)` / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML; the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed. - **All spec components render**: `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, `COLOR` (layout-greedy: `flex:1;align-self:stretch`), `SHAPE` (CSS/SVG by `SHAPE_KIND`), `DIVIDER`, `SPACER` (inline `flex:1`), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` (`data-min`/`data-max` ride on the gauge so the DOM client can recompute its percentage), `VSTACK`/ `HSTACK`/`LAZY_VSTACK`/`LAZY_HSTACK` (flex), `ZSTACK` (overlay), `GRID`/ `LAZY_VGRID`/`LAZY_HGRID` (CSS grid), `SCROLLVIEW`, `BUTTON`, `TEXT_FIELD` (incl. `IS_SECURE` → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR`, `TOGGLE` (`TOGGLE_STYLE`), `SLIDER`, `STEPPER` (the `.pathland-stepper` composite with `data-min`/`data-max`/`data-step` on its hidden range span), `DATE_PICKER` (`SET_DATE` → `days_to_date`), `PICKER` (option children rendered as `<option data-pathland-id="{child}" value="{index}">` + `SELECTION`), `MENU` (the `.pathland-menu` composite: `.pathland-menu-trigger` label + `.pathland-menu-items` children), `COLOR_PICKER`, `COMMENT`. - **Native elements** (the specs carry no renderer mappings — this is the concrete HTML map the removed spec hints lived in): `TEXT` → `<span>` (or `<p>`/`<h1>`–`<h5>` by `ROLE`/heading `TEXT_STYLE`), `IMAGE` → `<img>`, `ICON` → inline **Remix (filled)** `<svg class="pathland-icon">` (the canonical `ICON_NAME` resolves to its filled SVG markup via this renderer's own `icons` module (`crate::icons`, the web owner of the mapping); the svg carries `data-pathland-icon="<name>"` — the DOM client's lazy resolver reads it as an embedded glyph for instant on-page swaps; `LABEL` → `role="img"` + `aria-label`, none → `aria-hidden`; sized `1em` so `FONT_SIZE` scales it, tinted via `fill="currentColor"`), `SIZE_THAT_FITS` → `<div class="pathland-ftf">` (the fit slot: fill-sized with `data-pathland-fit` mirroring the `FIT_QUERY` LIST, decoded as `[count][f32×count]` at decode time — the DOM client derives the fit locally and reports `FIT_CHANGED` on transitions; the slot is layout-transparent, forwarding the parent flex container's `flex-direction`/`align-items`/`justify-content` (`inherit`) into its own box so a wrapper never pins a centered candidate to the start — `VStack(CENTER)` > fit slot > `HSTACK` keeps centering; stays size-taking via `flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;min-width/height:0`), and the **web-SSR snapshot form** (issue #141: the slot carries EVERY candidate, in `FIT_QUERY` order — the protocol's candidate-identity contract) renders each branch in a `data-pathland-fit-cand="i" data-pathland-fit-cand-id="<child>"` gate wrapper whose inline `display` is the pre-CSS default (candidate 0 `contents`, every other candidate `none`), marks the slot as the query context (`container-type:inline-size; container-name:pf-<id>`), and emits the `@container` **band rules** into a `<style data-pathland-fit>` head element: for each distinct threshold `T_i` (`i ≥ 1`, ascending) a self-contained `@container pf-<id> (min-width: T_i)` band that **hides every candidate `j ≠ i` and shows candidate `i`**, so the highest matching band wins and **exactly one** candidate is visible at any width (no band for `T_0`; below the first band the inline default shows candidate 0). A no-JS first paint therefore already shows the candidate matching the slot's width; the single-child live form is unchanged. The bands are **SSR-only** — the first `FIT_CHANGED` collapses the slot to the live single-child form and the DOM client removes the gating (`collapseFitSlotFor` unwraps the gate wrappers, strips the container/candidate attrs, and `dropFitBandRules` deletes the slot's rules)), `COLOR` → `<div>`, `SHAPE` → CSS shapes / inline SVG, `DIVIDER` → `<hr>`, `SPACER` → inline flex filler, `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `<progress>` / `.pathland-spinner`, `GAUGE` → `.pathland-gauge`, stacks/lazy stacks → flex `div`, `ZSTACK` → grid overlay `div`, grids → CSS-grid `div`, `SCROLLVIEW` → overflow `div` (**gap: `SCROLL_AXIS` 0x0021 not yet implemented** — still both-axis greedy), `BUTTON` → `<button>`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `<input>` (secure → `type="password"`), `TEXT_EDITOR` → `<textarea>`, `TOGGLE` → checkbox/switch input, `SLIDER` → `<input type="range">`, `STEPPER` → `.pathland-stepper`, `DATE_PICKER` → `<input type="date">`/`<input type="time">`, `PICKER` → `<select>` + `<option>`, `MENU` → `.pathland-menu` composite, `COLOR_PICKER` → `<input type="color">`, `VIDEO` → `<video controls>`, `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` → an off-flow (`position:absolute;1px;opacity:0`) shell (non-visual, layout-transparent — **not** `display:none`, which silences the `<video>`'s audio), `COMMENT` → none. - **Media (spec/MEDIA.md)**: `IMAGE` renders `<img src alt>` (the `LABEL` accessibility text is the `alt`; empty = decorative) and honors `CONTENT_MODE`/`ASPECT_RATIO` inline (`Fit`→`object-fit:contain`, `Fill`→`object-fit:cover`); a `VIDEO` surface renders `<video data-pathland-controller="C" controls>` (the binding attribute appears only when the surface references a controller). **Audio has no view.** A **`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`** is non-visual and layout-transparent: it renders an off-flow shell carrying the resource (`data-pathland-media-controller` + `data-pathland-media-src`), which the DOM client turns into the playback (keyed by the controller id; spec/EVENTS.md Media). Asset refs are absolute (`/_pathland/assets/…`); bytes never ride the opcode stream. - **Composite override mode**: `BUTTON`/`TOGGLE`/`SLIDER` with children render the custom body wrapped in the native element. - **Native browser controls inherit the design system**: the Tailwind-derived preflight stays the base reset, and every native form control carries a `pathland-*` class styled from design tokens: - text fields/editors: `.pathland-input.pathland-control`; - `PICKER` → `.pathland-select.pathland-control` (native dropdown arrow kept, tokenized field + options); - `DATE_PICKER` / `COLOR_PICKER` → `.pathland-date` / `.pathland-color` with `.pathland-control` (tokenized surface, inherited `color-scheme`, `accent-color`); - `SLIDER` → `.pathland-slider` with a renderer-owned track/thumb (`slider.track` / `slider.accent` / `slider.thumb`), no native range chrome; the `--pl-slider-fill` custom property is emitted inline for first paint and kept in sync by the DOM client (value/min/max/input). The native range input remains for keyboard/pointer interaction and accessibility; - `PROGRESS_VIEW` → `.pathland-progress` with tokenized WebKit/Mozilla track/fill pseudo-elements; - `VIDEO` → `.pathland-video` (and `.pathland-media` for custom bodies) with surface/radius/accent tokens. Inline opcode properties still override the base classes. Native `<select>` popups, date/color dialogs, and `<video>` controls remain UA shadow DOM, so their internals are best-effort; app-driven media is fully themeable. - **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis **position** — the default is hug (`flex-start`), never CSS `align-items:stretch`, per `spec/LAYOUT.md`; only `FILL`-sized children stretch via their `100%` size), `CONTENT_MARGINS`, `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL` → `width:100%`/`height:100%` expansion, `HUG` → intrinsic), the frame bounds `MIN_WIDTH`/`IDEAL_WIDTH`/`MAX_WIDTH` and the height equivalents (emitted on the SSR first paint, matching the DOM client), `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `TEXT_STYLE` (the renderer-owned default size/weight; explicit `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT` override), `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`, `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT` (positive → `-webkit-box`/`-webkit-line-clamp` **with `overflow:hidden`** — the clamp draws the ellipsis but does not clip on its own, so Safari would otherwise paint the overflowed text below the box, matching the DOM client), `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`, `BORDER_*`, `SELECTED`, `TOGGLE_STYLE`, `ENABLED`, `ROLE`/`STATE` (ARIA), plus `TEXT_CASE`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`/`STRIKETHROUGH`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`, `COLOR_INVERT`. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `HUG_CONTENT` (-2) is **omitted** (intrinsic size); `FILL` (-1) → `100%`. - **`SHADOW_*` (box-shadow)**: a non-zero `SHADOW_RADIUS` (or an `SHADOW_X`/`SHADOW_Y` offset) emits `box-shadow: <color> <x>px <y>px <radius>px` (color first — the canonical order a browser serializes back to, so the SSR string matches the hydrated DOM). The color is `SHADOW_COLOR` when set, else the **renderer-owned default `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`** — so a `shadow(radius)` modifier (radius only; the color is renderer-owned) already draws before hydration, matching the DOM client. - **`Z_INDEX` (draw-order override)**: a `ZSTACK` child's `Z_INDEX` is emitted on its **shell** (the grid item that participates in stacking — the child's own `z-index` is inert inside the shell), so a higher value draws above lower siblings regardless of child index (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §ZStack). **Every shell carries an explicit `z-index`** (the child's `Z_INDEX`, else `0`) and the ZStack container sets `isolation:isolate`, so overlapping grid items paint deterministically in every browser (WebKit paints a non-fill grid item below a full-area sibling when both are `z-index:auto`). Mirrored by the DOM client's `applyLayout`. - **Layout contract (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: cross-axis default is **hug** (`flex-start`), not CSS stretch; `ALIGNMENT` positions only (`Fill`=3 → hug default). `DIVIDER` is greedy on the cross axis (`width:100%`); `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy on both axes (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`); fixed frames emit exact px boxes. Conformance cases C1–C6 asserted in `lib.rs` tests. - **Fill propagation (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model)**: implemented — `fills_axis` resolves a Hug stack/ZStack containing a `FILL` child / greedy primitive on an axis as `FILL`, emitting `width/height:100%` on that axis, and cross-axis `FILL` children stretch via `align-self:stretch` (SSR + TS DOM client, kept canonical via the layout pass in `applyLayout`). - **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — an overlapping grid (`grid-area:1/1` cells); the container hugs to its largest child (`max-content`) unless Fixed/FILL (or fill propagation → `100%`); each child keeps its own size and is positioned by `ALIGNMENT` on both axes (SSR + TS DOM client). **Grid tracks are `minmax(0,1fr)`** (ZStack + count-generated grid tracks, `repeat(n,minmax(0,1fr))`, and lazy-hgrid auto columns), so a FILL ZStack/grid can shrink below its content min-height on a short viewport — an `end`-aligned child (e.g. a player bar) stays pinned instead of being pushed out of view and the inner `ScrollView` scrolls. A `GRID_TRACKS` per-track spec is emitted verbatim (app-authored). **Child shells carry no explicit `width/height`** — `justify-self/align-self:stretch` only applies when a grid item's size is `auto`, so pinning `max-content` silently degraded `stretch` to `start` and a FILL child's `100%` resolved circularly (content height), overflowing the viewport. With `auto` sizes a FILL child genuinely stretches to its (shrinkable) track and a Hug child keeps content size + alignment. - **ARIA ROLE/STATE maps match the DOM client**: the full `ROLE` set (button… menu, incl. `text`/`img`/`radio`/`spinbutton`/`tablist`/`list`/`grid`/ `region`/`menu`) and the `STATE` semantics (one true `aria-*` per state) are canonical with `lib/typescript/src/classes.ts`. - **Semantic HTML elements from `ROLE` + typography** (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties): a semantic role retags a **generic `div`/`span` shell** to its native element — `HEADER`→`<h2>`, `PARAGRAPH`→`<p>`, `LIST`→`<ul>`, `LIST_ITEM`→`<li>`, `SUMMARY`→`<section>`, and the landmarks `BANNER`→ `<header>`, `NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `MAIN`→`<main>`, `CONTENT_INFO`→`<footer>`, `COMPLEMENTARY`→`<aside>`, `ARTICLE`→`<article>`, `SECTION`→`<section>`, `SEARCH`→`<search>`. **Control components keep their native element** and emit no ARIA role from `ROLE` (`BUTTON` stays a `<button>`, `MENU` renders its intrinsic `role="menu"`). **Headings** come from a heading `TEXT_STYLE` typography (LargeTitle…Headline → `<h1>`–`<h5>`, always a heading) or from `ROLE_HEADER` (default `<h2>`); non-heading text defaults to `<span>`. Interactive/control roles are NOT in the catalog (intrinsic to the components); a custom button uses `Button`+`ButtonStyle`. The mapping lives in **`src/role_spec.rs`** (canonical with the DOM client — `pathland-ts-codegen` emits `generated/role-spec.ts`), with the role codes centralized in `pathland_core::constants::role`. - **`TREE::INSERT_CHILD` honors its `C` index** (`u32::MAX` = append), matching the protocol and the DOM client's `insertAt`. - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` / `data-binding-id` attributes. - **Navigation slot attrs** (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md): a slot node's `ROUTE` (STRING) renders as `data-pathland-route="<path>"`, its `TRANSITION` hint renders as `data-pathland-transition="<platform|fade|slide|scale>"`, its `NAV_CHROME` (F32 enum) renders `data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"` when `Custom` (the renderer adds no default chrome), and `NAV_DEPTH` (U32) renders `data-pathland-depth="N"` when deeper than its root so the DOM client can hydrate its default back button from the SSR HTML — the DOM renderer mirrors the route into the URL, may animate a swap, and draws the renderer's own back button (the web has no native navigation container). - `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time). - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**: - The naming/length conventions live in **`src/token_spec.rs`** — the single source of truth consumed by the renderer AND by `pathland-ts-codegen`, which emits the DOM client's `lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts` (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef`). - `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme. - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`). - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`): a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` with `valueType = STRING` resolves the value string from the batch's string section and emits it single-quoted (escaped) as a `:root` rule (or inside the dark media query). - The override rules render inside their own **`<style data-pathland-tokens>`** element in the document head, **after** the built-in block (so their `:root` variables win the cascade and the browser applies them) — matching the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides → no extra element. - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the renderer. - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`, the **shared control core** (`--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*`), and the component tokens (`--pl-toggle-*`, `--pl-slider-*`, `--pl-progress-*`, `--pl-gauge-*`, `--pl-stepper-*`, `--pl-picker-*`, `--pl-menu-*`, `--pl-label-*`, `--pl-size-control-*`), all with light + dark values. `.pathland-*` rules reference the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components. - **Forced scheme**: `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` sets `data-pathland-scheme` on `<html>`; the platform-dark media rule is scoped to `:root:not([data-pathland-scheme])` and the dark values are repeated under `:root[data-pathland-scheme="dark"]`. Forced light suppresses the media rule. `META::RESET_THEME` clears the batch's overrides. - **Explicit `dark.` references** resolve to the forced-dark variable family (`--pl-dark-…`), so they use the dark value in either scheme. - **Unknown/unresolved token fallback**: `var(--pl-…, unset)` so the renderer's own default styling applies. Base overrides are repeated in the dark scope so they correctly outrank built-in dark defaults (dark override → base override → dark default). ## Built-in HTML base design (`design/`) The built-in stylesheet is now **generated**, not hand-written in `css.rs`: - `design/tokens/{base,semantic,component}` is a three-layer Style Dictionary source (flat DTCG entries). Base literals are compiled into literals and never emitted; semantic + component tokens are emitted in four layers (`:root`, platform-dark media, forced-dark/light scheme selectors, and the `--pl-dark-*` forced-dark family). - `design/html/{reset,components}.css` holds the hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` rules. Component rules consume `var(--pl-*)` tokens; no design-relevant literal remains (sizes, radii, border widths, durations, z-index, focus rings, opacities). - `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs` provide build/watch/validation. `check` verifies Tier-1 catalog coverage, layer/reference direction, dark/forced-dark declarations, `$extensions.pathland.internal` markings, and that every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by `token_spec::isLengthToken`. - `design/build/base.css` + `base.css.name` (the SHA-256 content hash, e.g. `base-5f86423db422.css`) are synced to `assets/` by `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` (and `--check` fails on drift). `src/css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!`; `builtin_css()` / `builtin_css_name()` expose them and `STYLE` wraps the bundle in `<style>`. - **External stylesheet mode**: `render_document` stays inline (the library default); `render_document_linked(opcodes, strings, root, css_base)` emits `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{css_base}/{name}">` instead. Token overrides and fit-band rules stay inline after it. The C ABI adds `pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`, and `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java port + Spring/Quarkus starters expose them and serve the CSS immutable. An empty base falls back to inline. - The design bundle is wired into the Maven `refresh-ide` profile and a CI design job that runs build/check/sync-check. ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist: - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`), including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment, text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds, hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**. - **`css::STYLE`** is the generated built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document` (see "Built-in HTML base design" above), containing: - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`), - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`, `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/ placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer, - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/ disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`, focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens; `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so native form controls and the page follow the theme. - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` / `_free`, plus `pathland_html_icon_svg`) for non-JVM cross-language hosts (Swift/.NET/…; the JVM uses the pure-Java port). `pathland_html_icon_svg(name)` returns the icon glyph's full `<svg>` (canonical name → glyph, unknown/extension → the renderer's fallback glyph) — how any host serves `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from ONE Rust source (the DOM client's lazy icon fetch) instead of per-platform static files. The `_tailwind_compile` entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`, `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**. Non-JVM hosts that embed the cdylib must refresh it with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` (not just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the shared library). The JVM no longer embeds it; `GoldenConformanceTest` guards the Java port against golden-fixture drift. - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors, strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`). ## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift) The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated (`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the contract both renderers must satisfy. ## Not implemented / gaps - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (spec/LAYOUT.md §content fitting): aligned — it **alone** has no observable effect (the old `nowrap`+`text-overflow:ellipsis` emission is gone, SSR + TS DOM client); under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp the renderer tail- ellipsizes via `line-clamp`. Renderer-owned fidelity: CSS cannot place a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to the tail ellipsis. - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding/content margins, corner radius, opacity, width/height, border width/color, shadow color/x/y/radius). **Parent-path fallback and per-component native control chrome are not implemented in CSS** (see the gaps above). - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**: grids emit `gap` from `SPACING`, equal-`1fr` track templates from the `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/ LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/ `minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, taking precedence over the count), and **per-cell alignment** — each cell is wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell, else the grid `ALIGNMENT` position (default start) — with `justify-items`/ `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`) and renders **only its first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C14 covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. the `gridrow` scenario). - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property). - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact. - **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web. - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — no external/webfont loading, so the rendered document makes no network requests for fonts and works offline. An app can still pick its own typeface via a `font.body.family` `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override (any STRING value, e.g. `"Inter"` if the app hosts it). - Compound token refs cover shadow x/y/radius and border width (the DOM client mirrors them); per-component tokens still style only the component CSS the renderer owns. ## Verified by `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 77 headless render tests (components, properties, composite, event attrs, navigation slot route/transition attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames, inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). The built-in CSS tests assert the generated bundle is embedded (reset, tokens, component rules) and that component rules reference the catalog/metadata tokens; the linked-mode tests assert the hashed `<link>` and that the default render remains inline. `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard. `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check` and `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` validate the design pipeline and the committed bundle.

result.output: # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native library). Protocol contract: `spec/`. ## Implemented - **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` / `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes. - **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario. - **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root, meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`). Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's `document_meta.document.html` fixture. - **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants, `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and size-that-fits snapshots. - **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` / `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed ``; `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving. - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers. - **Icon glyphs**: `iconSvg(name)` returns the full inline `identity (the `uiId` map key) is deliberately separate from the persisted-state scope (the client's `wid`, carried only on the WebSocket URL — never in the page URL, so the address bar stays clean). The SSR request therefore has no `wid`: `renderHtml(route, wid)` with a null `wid` renders defaults; the client's live session is scoped by the WS `wid`, and a same-tab reload re-syncs that window's persisted state over the WebSocket. The old `session` cookie is removed. - **`PathlandSession`** — per-session: builds the `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal, mounts `app.newRoot().modifiers(environmentBinding(e -> e.key(ACTIVE_PATH).value(activePath)))`, **delta-batched send-on-`endFrame`** (`DeltaBatcher` coalesces per-signal frames into one batch — flush ~20 ms or 16 KB, string offsets rebased — so a continuous input burst can't overflow a remote WebSocket send queue), `applyEnvironment` (re-route guard-aware via the bound router), `dispatch` (tap/nav-intent/text/value/date/NAVIGATE), `resync`, `renderHtml`, `close`. Runtime theming: `setTheme(ThemeData)`, `resetTheme()`, and `setColorScheme(ThemeMode)` emit one `META::RESET_THEME` + `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` frame or `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` to the live client (renderer state; no tree re-emission). The SSR document keeps the mount theme until a resync/reload. `sendBatch` drops the connection on any send failure (a client reconnect then re-syncs via `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket); `closeConnection` best-effort closes an `AutoCloseable` adapter (the starters now close their underlying WebSocket on failure). Now takes the app's `base` and `stateScope` explicitly (the registry supplies them). - **`DeltaBatcher`** — merges session delta frames (opcodes + a single rebased string section) and flushes as one network batch on a timer/byte threshold; the Java analogue of the Rust transport's `Batcher`. It owns the per-session **message sequence** (stamped on each flushed batch via `FrameCodec.encodeFrame(frame, sequence)`) so the DOM client can detect a lost batch and recover with `META::RESYNC` (spec/OPCODE.md §Sequence gap detection); an empty flush consumes no sequence. The **sender runs OUTSIDE the monitor** — a blocking/queueing send can never stall the actor thread's `append` or the flush scheduler. Coalescing tests cover merging + rebasing, a 100-frame burst collapsing to one send, incrementing sequences, and a blocking sender not holding the lock. - **`PathlandConnection`** — the transport seam (`send(byte[])`/`isOpen()`); each starter adapts its WebSocket type to it. - **Observability seam** — `PathlandTelemetry` (default `NOOP`): the runtime emits session open/close, inbound event batches, inbound drops (oversize/rate), flushed batches (frames/opcodes/bytes + merge-encode time), SSR render latency, resync requests, and send failures; the host binds a pull-based active-sessions gauge. `PathlandHost`/`PathlandRegistry`/ `PathlandSession`/`DeltaBatcher` thread it through (a host with no telemetry pays nothing). This module also ships the `dev.pathland.observability` Micrometer + OpenTelemetry adapters; the starters auto-wire them. Logging is **SLF4J** (both frameworks bind it) — the old ad-hoc `System.out` is gone. See issue #62. - **Concurrency stress** — `RegistryConcurrencyTest`: 100 sessions driven through the registry concurrently (clicks on each session's button) while SSR-style requests construct throwaway sessions on request threads — the shared-actor / global-`Scheduler` cross-session corruption guard. Each session must reach exactly its own click count (no lost effects, no cross-session values). - **Shared WS test harness** — `dev.pathland.server.test.{WsSession,MultiSessionProbe}` (a JDK-WebSocket client speaking the PLPL protocol: env/resync/click/ping) lives in this module in main scope, so package builds resolve it as a normal jar; the starters' 100-session stress tests reuse it. - **`StateStores`** — default state store: Redis when reachable, else the supplied fallback. The `dev.pathland.state.redis.RedisStateStore` (Lettuce) ships in this module too. - **Observability adapters** — `dev.pathland.observability.MicrometerTelemetry` turns the seam into `pathland.*` meters (counters, timers, a distribution summary, a pull-based sessions gauge, every meter tagged by `mount`); the optional `TracingTelemetry` decorator emits an OpenTelemetry span per frame send / inbound event batch / SSR render. Micrometer is a compile dependency; the OTel API is `optional`, so a host that does not enable tracing pays nothing. - **SSR debug comments (property-gated)**: `PathlandSession`/`PathlandRegistry` take a `debugHtml` flag (constructor + `isDebugHtml()`); when set, `renderHtml` uses the renderer's debug mode so every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component and the modifiers applied. The Spring/Quarkus starters bind it to the `pathland.debug-html` property (default `false`). - **Reserved framework root**: `PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE` (`/_pathland`) — the SSR page carries the app's base as `data-pathland-base` and the DOM-client bundle is injected at `{base}/dom-renderer-.js` (`PathlandAssets` reads the current name from the `_pathland/dom-renderer.current` manifest on the classpath, resolving through the thread context classloader first so a Quarkus extension parent loader can see the application's static resources; it falls back to the literal `dom-renderer.js` only when absent) so the client's WebSocket and asset refs resolve from the same reserved prefix (spec DSL.md). The content-hashed name busts the immutable asset cache with a fresh URL per build. The built-in base design is linked the same way: `renderHtml` renders through `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked(frame, root, base)`, so the CSS href is `{base}/base-.css` (token overrides/fit rules stay inline). Multi-app hosts give each mount its own base. - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `PathlandHost` carries a host-level `serviceWorker` flag (default `false`; one registration covers the whole origin) threaded to every `PathlandRegistry`; `PathlandSession.renderHtml` emits `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` on `` when set, and the DOM client registers `{base}/sw.js` (root scope) / unregisters when absent (the kill switch). `PathlandRegistry.serviceWorkerUrl()` names the served script. `renderHtml` also emits `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"` when the request carried a real per-window id, so the client can skip its initial `META::RESYNC` (the SSR was already rendered with that window's state and the live session shares it). ## Not implemented / gaps - No multi-node/shared sessions (each server owns its sessions in-memory). - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC`, **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. While an SSR snapshot is pending, `awaitSnapshot` retries `META::RESYNC` every 500 ms, so a lost first handshake cannot consume the whole SSR budget. The service credential + a cycle-guard instance id ride the handshake headers. **Backpressure** (spec/PROXY.md §8): a "chatty origin" breaker (a per-second batch cap → drop + `RESYNC`) and event coalescing (pointer-moves coalesce by target; discrete events flush immediately). - **`proxy.ProxyHost`** — one `ProxySession` per `PROXY_VIEW` node, each with its own block; routes inbound events whose target is in a proxy range to the owning origin connection; owns the proxy scheduler. `reconcile(wanted)` starts a session for every `PROXY_VIEW` node and closes the session of every node that left the tree; released id blocks go to a **free-block pool** and are reused, so repeated removal/re-add cycles never exhaust the 1024-block range. - **`PathlandSession`** integration — captures `RenderResult.proxyViews()` and registers the emitter's structural-reconcile callback (`Emitter.onStructureReconciled`) to `reconcileProxies()`, so a proxy lives **exactly while its node is in the retained tree** (spec/PROXY.md §7): a `SizeThatFits` slot dropping the candidate that held it closes the origin connection, and re-adding it opens a fresh one (re-seeded by `META::RESYNC`). The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not in the DOM); eliminating it needs the `ProxySession` to track the ids it emitted and `DELETE` them on close. ## Verified by `mvn test` — `PathlandSessionTest`: mounts + routes taps through the binding maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other), and **message-before-open ordering** (environment/resync that race `open` still attach the connection and emit the snapshot). `PathlandHostTest`: longest-prefix dispatch + route stripping, mount-boundary respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxyIdMapTest`: the reserved range, block round-trips, overflow rejection, and the opcode remap (TREE/PARAMETER node ids remapped, APPEND/META untouched, EVENT targets unmapped). `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC handshake + handshake headers, snapshot retry when the first RESYNC is lost, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame rebases its string offsets (SET_TEXT / LIST / STRING operands) and returns the base unchanged when there is nothing to append.--- # pathland-quarkus — implementation status **Last updated:** November 6, 2026 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin` capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`. ## Implemented - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`: `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes), `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout, reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`. `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance. - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly, Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults; application config (including `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins. - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount. - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt. - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry; `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`. - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session). - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps: the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment. Same stateless rule as the root socket. - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead) dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped); SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS); per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS. **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`** serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`. - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`) to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`. - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see. - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) + `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear at `/q/metrics`. - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`. Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued), and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection / a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it). - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG` **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat. - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`) no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed). - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension. - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. # Deploying the Quarkus SSR demo

Runs the [Pathland Quarkus demo](pathland-quarkus-demo/) (server-side HTML at any
path + live `/ws` deltas) as a container — the application evidence for the Restack
proposal (issue #71, `docs/PREAPPLICATION-TODO.md`).

The image is multi-stage: it builds the Java reactor (the HTML renderer and
inline-Markdown parser are pure-Java ports), packages the Quarkus app, and runs
it on a JRE 17 runtime. No Rust toolchain or native library is needed.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the Java reactor plus
the generated base-design assets under
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The image's Maven step selects both `pathland-quarkus-demo` and
`pathland-quarkus-deployment`. The deployment module is not a Maven dependency of
the demo, but the runtime extension descriptor validates its dependencies against
it; omitting it makes a fresh (empty `~/.m2`) build fail Quarkus extension
verification.

## Run locally

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 pathland-quarkus-demo
# → http://localhost:8080
```

A quick check that it serves:

```bash
curl -I http://localhost:8080/          # 200, text/html
curl http://localhost:8080/ | grep -o 'data-pathland-id'   # hydrated SSR markup
curl -sSI https://<host>/ | grep -i '^strict-transport-security'   # HSTS
```

HSTS is app-owned (the extension does not default it): the demo sets
`max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` in its `application.properties`. Because
that file is baked into the image, changing it requires a rebuild/redeploy — a
plain restart of an existing container will not pick it up.

State defaults to the in-memory store (no Redis needed for the demo). To use
Redis, pass a `REDIS_URL` and the Redis `StateStore` in `pathland-server-core` is
selected at runtime — the standalone demo runs without it.

## Push to a registry

```bash
docker tag pathland-quarkus-demo ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
docker push ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
```

## Deploy to a host

Any platform that runs a Docker container exposing TCP 8080 works:

- **Railway / Fly.io** — point at the image (or use a Dockerfile deploy); set the
  public port to **8080**. The app binds `0.0.0.0` (see
  `application.properties`).
- **Hetzner / any VPS** — `docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name pathland pathland-quarkus-demo`
  (optionally behind Caddy/nginx; forward `GET /` and the WebSocket `Upgrade`).
- **Platform port override** — the app honors `QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT` if a platform
  assigns a different port.

### Requirements

- **WebSocket support**: the demo keeps the first page live via `/ws` (raw-input
  events + `PLPL` deltas). The reverse proxy / load balancer must forward the
  WebSocket `Upgrade` headers; most PaaS do this by default.
- **Health check**: `GET /` returning 200 with HTML is the simplest probe. The
  container has no separate health endpoint.
- **Memory**: the JVM is capped at 256 MB (`-Xmx256m`); the demo is small.

content.text:
Short version: the **marketing shell is buildable today** with the Kotlin DSL (hero, feature grid, screenshots, video, CTA, footer). The missing piece is a **block-Markdown content layer that emits Kotlin DSL views**, plus a few renderer primitives that rich docs need.

## What already works

- Kotlin DSL has `Text` (inline Markdown), `Image`, stacks, `Grid`/`GridRow`, `ScrollView`, `Divider`, fonts/text styles, colors, frames, borders, padding, links, and `ViewThatFits` for responsive layouts.
- `Router`/`NavigationLink` support multi-page docs; `windowMetadata` and `PageMetadata` cover titles/SEO.
- Quarkus/Spring SSR + live deltas, per-route canonical/OG/JSON-LD, assets, and a container deploy path already exist.
- Semantic HTML roles cover headings (`h1`–`h5`), paragraphs, lists, nav/main/article, etc.

## What we lack

### 1. Block-level Markdown (the main gap)

`dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is **inline only** — bold, italic, code spans, strikethrough, links (`lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/markdown/Markdown.java:19`). It explicitly excludes block Markdown, images, and references.

Missing:

- headings, paragraphs, ordered/unordered/nested lists
- fenced code blocks
- blockquotes, thematic breaks
- GFM tables
- images (`![alt](src)` currently becomes literal `!` + a link)
- autolinks, hard breaks, reference links, task lists, footnotes
- a block AST, heading IDs, slug generation, and TOC extraction
- a Kotlin DSL entry point such as `Markdown(text)` / `MarkdownPage(text)` that maps blocks to DSL views

This is app-side, not a protocol change. The parser and renderer must live in Kotlin/JVM and emit `View` trees; do not render Markdown to HTML separately.

### 2. Renderer/protocol gaps for docs

These are the places where the current protocol makes proper docs awkward:

- **Code blocks cannot preserve whitespace.** There is no `WHITE_SPACE`/`pre` property, so HTML collapses newlines and indentation. A correct fix is a small `WHITE_SPACE` property (`normal`/`nowrap`/`pre`/`pre-wrap`) plus a Kotlin modifier, and updates to Rust/Java/TS renderers. A `CODE_BLOCK` primitive would also work but is heavier.
- **Headings cannot be deep-linked.** There is no HTML `id`/anchor property. TOC links and `#section` URLs need an `ANCHOR`/`ELEMENT_ID` string property rendered as `id` on the heading, plus DOM-client support.
- **Tables have no semantics.** `Grid` can lay out a grid, but there are no `TABLE`/`ROW`/`COLUMN_HEADER`/`CELL` roles in the role catalog (`Roles.kt` stops at `SEARCH`). We can build a `Table` from `VStack`/`HStack` visually, but proper accessibility needs new ARIA roles or a table primitive.
- **List markers are reset away.** `LIST`/`LIST_ITEM` map to `<ul>/<li>`, but the reset sets `list-style: none` (`design/html/reset.css:31`) and there is no ordered-list numbering. The DSL must render bullet/number labels explicitly, or we add renderer list CSS.
- **Only `h1`–`h5` exist.** Markdown `h6` needs a mapping decision (probably `h6` → `h5` or a new heading-level property).
- **Syntax highlighting has no theme tokens.** `AttributedString` supports color runs, so highlighting is possible, but we need `color.code.*` design tokens for light/dark and a highlighter. We also need to decide whether to ship a small built-in lexer or use a JVM library.
- **No copy-code action.** A copy button is a client-side clipboard operation; the protocol currently has no client action for it. Optional, but expected in docs.
- **In-page anchor scrolling after client-side route changes** needs handling; browser default works on full SSR navigation.

### 3. Docs-site plumbing

- **No docs layout kit**: sidebar, TOC, breadcrumbs, prev/next, mobile drawer, search. These are buildable with existing DSL primitives, but need to be written.
- **No search**: need an index built from the Markdown AST and a signal-driven results UI. Server-driven search over the WebSocket is the simplest Kotlin-DSL approach.
- **Sitemap is root-only** (`IndexResource.java:92`); a docs site needs a generated multi-route sitemap.
- **No static export**: the site is SSR/server-rendered only. If you want GitHub Pages/Cloudflare Pages, we need an export/pre-render step; otherwise deploy the Quarkus container.
- **Asset route** exists for demo assets, but docs need a clear convention for screenshots/images (bundled resources or an asset route).
- **Content source**: large docs in Kotlin triple-quoted strings are unwieldy. I would load `.md` resources and pass them through the Kotlin DSL renderer — the rendering still happens entirely via the DSL.

## Proposed implementation plan

1. **Markdown content layer**
   - New JVM module (e.g. `lib/java/pathland-markdown` or `pathland-docs`) containing a block parser + AST.
   - Reuse the existing inline parser for inline runs; add images/link handling as needed.
   - DSL API: `Markdown(source, options)`, `MarkdownPage(page)`, with `MarkdownOptions` for heading IDs, link resolution, highlighting, image base.
   - Block mapping: headings → `Text` + heading style/anchor; paragraphs → `Text`; lists → nested `VStack`/`HStack` with markers; code → code block view; quotes → bordered container; tables → `Table`; images → `Image` + `LABEL`; rules → `Divider`.
   - Build TOC from the AST.

2. **Renderer/protocol additions**
   - Add `WHITE_SPACE` and `ANCHOR`/`ELEMENT_ID` properties (spec-first: `spec/OPCODE.md`, constants, `protocol.tsv`, Java constants, Rust/Java/TS renderers, golden fixtures).
   - Add table ARIA roles or a `Table` primitive decision.
   - Add `color.code.*` design tokens and a Kotlin `CodeBlock` component.
   - Update `status.md` files for every affected project.

3. **Docs site shell**
   - `DocsLayout` (header, sidebar, content, TOC, prev/next), responsive via `ViewThatFits`.
   - `DocsSite` router with one route per page, route-aware metadata, generated sitemap.
   - Search index + results page.
   - Kotlin-authored Quarkus docs demo/module with `.md` resources and image assets.

4. **Marketing site**
   - Landing page in the Kotlin DSL using existing components; link to docs.
   - Theme/token polish and screenshots/video.

5. **Testing**
   - Parser/AST unit tests and block-rendering golden tests.
   - HTML/SSR fixtures; accessibility assertions for headings, lists, tables, alt text.
   - Kotlin DSL tests; `mvn install`, design build/check/sync, and Rust golden/manifest regeneration if protocol constants change.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **Markdown source**: `.md` resources loaded by the Kotlin DSL (recommended), or Kotlin triple-quoted strings only?
2. **Parser**: use `commonmark-java` + GFM tables (robust, one dependency), or hand-roll a GFM subset to keep the JVM side dependency-free?
3. **Protocol additions**: are `WHITE_SPACE`, `ANCHOR`, and table roles acceptable, or must everything stay app-only with workarounds?
4. **Scope**: is syntax highlighting required in v1? And do you want server-side search now or later?
1: yes, .md 2: yes, and can it be reused for the textview even if it allows less markdeown? 3: white_space and anchor is ok, but defer table 4: search is later

# Plan: Pathland marketing site + docs site in the Kotlin DSL

## Decisions locked in

- Docs content lives as `.md` resources.
- Use `commonmark-java` (0.24.0) as the parser, with GFM tables and strikethrough. It is used **only as an AST parser** — never its HTML renderer.
- `Text` may reuse the same parser in a restricted **inline-only mode**. I would gate it with a parity suite; if a case cannot be reconciled with the existing Rust/JVM golden contract, keep the current inline parser for `Text` and use commonmark only for docs.
- Add `WHITE_SPACE` and `ANCHOR` protocol properties.
- Defer table protocol roles; render GFM tables with existing DSL primitives and document the accessibility limitation.
- Search is out of scope for v1.

## Architecture

```
.md resources
   ↓ DocsRepository (frontmatter, routes, nav, TOC)
Kotlin docs DSL (Markdown/CodeBlock/Table/DocsLayout)
   ↓
Pathland opcodes
   ↓
HTML SSR / DOM client / native renderers
```

New pieces:

- `lib/java/pathland-view-core`: commonmark-backed inline mode for `Text` (behind parity tests).
- `lib/java/pathland-docs`: a reusable Kotlin docs kit — block Markdown renderer, docs components, content loading, nav/TOC/SEO helpers.
- `lib/java/pathland-docs-demo`: a Quarkus site with marketing at `/`, docs at `/docs/...`, `.md` content, and image assets.

No Markdown-to-HTML shortcut. Every block becomes a Kotlin DSL `View`.

## Work items

### 1. CommonMark integration

Add to the Maven reactor:

- `org.commonmark:commonmark:0.24.0`
- `commonmark-ext-gfm-tables`
- `commonmark-ext-gfm-strikethrough`
- `commonmark-ext-yaml-front-matter`
- optionally `commonmark-ext-autolink`, `commonmark-ext-task-list-items`

Use commonmark for:

- block parsing in the docs module
- inline parsing within blocks, producing `AttributedString`
- raw HTML detection (render as escaped text; never execute raw HTML)

Do not use commonmark’s HTML renderer.

### 2. Reuse commonmark for `Text` (inline mode)

Keep the public `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` API (`parse`, `parseOrPlain`, `containsMarkdownSyntax`, `isAvailable`) but back it with commonmark:

- Parse with a restricted inline configuration: text, emphasis, strong, code, link, strikethrough, soft/hard breaks.
- Only accept a document whose top-level blocks are paragraphs; if headings/lists/code fences/etc. appear, fall back to plain text so `Text` remains inline-only and block markers stay literal.
- Flatten multiple paragraphs with `\n\n`.
- Inline images become alt text (or literal); raw HTML becomes literal text.
- Emit style runs in post-order so nested runs match the existing Rust/JVM order.
- Keep the bounded `parseOrPlain` cache and fast-path.

Add a parity test suite comparing the new inline output against the current parser for every case in `MarkdownTest` plus extra nested/UTF-8/code-span cases. If a case cannot match, retain the legacy parser for `Text` and use commonmark only for docs.

### 3. Block Markdown renderer (`pathland-docs`)

`Markdown(source: String, options: MarkdownOptions): View` maps:

| Markdown | Kotlin DSL output |
|---|---|
| Heading | `Text` + heading `Font` + `ANCHOR` + `ROLE_HEADER`; h6 → h5 |
| Paragraph | `Text(AttributedString)` + `ROLE_PARAGRAPH` |
| Bullet/ordered list | nested `VStack` of `HStack` rows; `•`/`1.` markers; `ROLE_LIST`/`ROLE_LIST_ITEM` |
| Task list | `☐`/`☑` markers (static) |
| Fenced code | `CodeBlock`: monospace, `WHITE_SPACE=PRE`, padding, background, border, horizontal `ScrollView` |
| Blockquote | `HStack` with a narrow `Rectangle` accent + nested markdown |
| Thematic break | `Divider` |
| GFM table | `Grid`/`GridRow` cells with header styling, per-cell alignment, horizontal scroll; no semantic table roles in v1 |
| Image | `Image` with `LABEL` = alt, `scaledToFit`, optional caption from title; block images only |
| Inline link | `AttributedString` link run; resolve relative `.md` links to routes |
| Raw HTML | escaped literal text or dropped |

`MarkdownOptions`:

- `headingIds` / `slugger`
- `linkResolver(sourcePath, href) -> String`
- `imageBase`
- `codeHighlighter: CodeHighlighter?` (default plain)
- `headingOffset`
- `allowRawHtml = false`

Also provide:

- `MarkdownToc.extract(page)` → heading list (level, id, text)
- a slugger with duplicate handling (`intro`, `intro-1`)
- a `CodeBlock` component
- a `Table` component (visual only in v1)
- an optional `Callout` component for `> [!NOTE]`-style blocks (phase 2)

### 4. Protocol changes: `WHITE_SPACE` + `ANCHOR`

**`WHITE_SPACE`**

- Enum: `Normal=0`, `NoWrap=1`, `Pre=2`, `PreWrap=3`.
- Renderer emits `white-space`.
- DSL modifier: `whiteSpace(WhiteSpace.PRE)` / `preserveWhitespace()`.
- Update spec, constants, `protocol.tsv`, Rust/Java/TS renderers, DOM client, Java constants, golden fixtures, `status.md`.

**`ANCHOR`**

- STRING property rendered as an HTML `id` on the node’s shell/heading.
- DSL modifier: `anchor("getting-started")`.
- Renderer/DOM client must both set and remove it.
- Used by headings and TOC links (`#getting-started`).

Follow the repo’s spec-first workflow:

1. `spec/OPCODE.md` / `spec/MODIFIERS.md`
2. `pathland-core` constants + manifest
3. Rust + Java renderers
4. TS DOM client
5. `cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest`
6. `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit`
7. `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`
8. update `status.md`

### 5. Content pipeline (`.md` resources)

`DocsRepository` model:

```kotlin
data class DocsPage(
    val sourcePath: String,
    val route: String,
    val title: String,
    val description: String?,
    val section: String?,
    val order: Int,
    val draft: Boolean,
    val markdown: String,
)
```

- Frontmatter fields: `title`, `description`, `route`, `order`, `section`, `draft`, `updated`, `image`.
- Route default: `content/docs/getting-started.md` → `/docs/getting-started`; `index.md` → `/docs` or its folder route.
- Navigation tree: sections + order.
- TOC: derived from headings.
- Prev/next: derived from the ordered page list.
- Link rewriting: relative `.md` links resolve through the repository; missing targets fail a build/test check.
- Production: read `META-INF/pathland-docs.index` generated at build time, then load resources from the jar.
- Dev: if `pathland.docs.content-dir` is set, scan the filesystem and reload changed files without a rebuild.
- Generate the index with a small build step (Maven `exec`/script) wired into `refresh-ide` and CI.

### 6. Docs layout and navigation

`DocsLayout` component:

- Header: brand/logo, top nav, GitHub link, mobile menu toggle.
- Desktop: sidebar (`ScrollView`, ~260px), content (`ScrollView`), TOC (~220px).
- Mobile: `ViewThatFits` or state-driven drawer; content only.
- Sidebar: section groups + `NavigationLink`s; active state via `isActive`.
- TOC: heading links using `Text("[label](#id)")` or `NavigationLink`.
- Breadcrumbs, prev/next links.
- Per-page `windowMetadata { title(...); description(...) }`.
- `PageMetadata` per route in `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` for canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD.

### 7. Sitemap and assets

- Extend `PathlandApp` (or a small `SitemapProvider` seam) with extra sitemap routes; update the Quarkus and Spring starters to append them instead of emitting a root-only sitemap.
- Serve docs images from `/docs-assets/...` (resources/static route or demo asset route).
- Keep the existing `/robots.txt`; it already points at the sitemap.
- No static export in v1 — deploy the Quarkus container. If static hosting is required later, add a pre-render/export step.

### 8. Marketing page

A Kotlin DSL landing page at `/`:

- hero, tagline, CTA buttons
- feature `Grid`
- screenshots via `Image`
- optional `Video`
- architecture/code snippets via `CodeBlock`
- footer linking to docs/GitHub

This is buildable with existing primitives; no new protocol surface needed.

### 9. Tests and verification

- `pathland-view-core`: inline commonmark parity against existing `MarkdownTest` and Rust-derived expectations.
- `pathland-docs`: parser fixtures for every block type; render each fixture through `HtmlRenderer` and assert headings/anchors, list markers, code whitespace, image alt, table structure, escaped raw HTML.
- Link resolver, slug uniqueness, frontmatter, nav ordering, prev/next, broken-link checks.
- Quarkus tests: `/`, `/docs/...`, metadata, sitemap, assets.
- Protocol: manifest, engine golden, HTML golden, TS conformance, Java conformance.
- Run `mvn install`, `cargo test`, design build/check/sync, and update all affected `status.md` files.

## Deferred

- table ARIA roles / semantic table primitive
- search index and search UI
- syntax highlighting implementation (keep the `CodeHighlighter` seam; ship plain monospace first)
- inline images in `AttributedString` (block images only)
- copy-code buttons (needs a client clipboard action)
- static-site export
- docs versioning
- footnotes/admonitions (optional follow-up)

## Open decision

Only one remains: **syntax highlighting in v1?** My recommendation is to ship v1 with plain monospace code blocks and the `CodeHighlighter` interface, then add highlighting as a focused follow-up (with `color.code.*` design tokens). If you want it in the first cut, the plan adds a small Kotlin tokenizer for Kotlin/Java/Rust/TS/JS/Shell/JSON/HTML/Markdown and the code token palette.
Just monospace, and then an issue for the syntax highligting with explanation of why it is needed.

Updated: v1 ships **plain monospace code blocks only**. No highlighter, no `color.code.*` tokens, and no extra parser dependency beyond commonmark. Syntax highlighting becomes a tracked follow-up issue.

## Plan delta

### Code blocks in v1

`CodeBlock` renders:

- literal code text from the fenced block
- `FONT_DESIGN = MONOSPACED`
- `WHITE_SPACE = PRE` (the new protocol property)
- padding, background, border, radius
- horizontal `ScrollView` for long lines
- optional language label from the fence info string

The language is used **only for the label**; it does not affect rendering. Unknown/absent languages render the same plain block. `MarkdownOptions` does not expose a highlighter in v1.

### Issue workflow

- Add “file the syntax-highlighting issue” as a first implementation step.
- The issue is separate from the docs-site v1 scope; the docs site does not depend on it.
- Once execution is approved, create it with `gh issue create` using the draft below.

## Issue draft

**Title:** Docs code blocks: add syntax highlighting in a follow-up

**Body:**

```markdown
## Context

The Pathland docs site renders Markdown fenced code blocks through the Kotlin
DSL. v1 deliberately ships plain monospace code blocks with preserved
whitespace (`WHITE_SPACE = PRE`), horizontal scrolling, and an optional language
label. This keeps the initial docs implementation small and avoids adding a
highlighter before the content pipeline is proven.

Code samples are central to Pathland's documentation: the protocol, opcode
layout, DSL usage, and every renderer/host example are expressed as code. Plain
monospace is readable, but it does not help readers scan a snippet or
distinguish keywords, strings, comments, types, and function names.

## Why this is needed

- **Comprehension:** highlighting makes structure visible at a glance, which
  matters for a protocol with compact binary layouts and multiple language
  bindings (Kotlin, Java, Rust, TypeScript, shell).
- **Error spotting:** color distinguishes strings from identifiers and comments,
  so malformed examples are easier to notice.
- **Cross-language comparison:** the same docs show Kotlin/Java/Rust/TS versions
  of the same API; consistent highlighting helps readers map concepts.
- **Docs quality:** highlighted code is a baseline expectation for developer
  documentation and makes the site feel finished.
- **Accessibility and theming:** semantic code tokens can be tuned for contrast
  in both light and dark schemes, instead of using ad-hoc literal colors.
- **No protocol gap:** `AttributedString` already supports color/style runs and
  every renderer already maps those runs to spans/CSS. The missing piece is the
  highlighter and design tokens, not new wire capability.

## What v1 has

- `CodeBlock` with monospace text, preserved whitespace, padding/background/
  border, horizontal scroll, and language label.
- `AttributedString` style runs (`TextAttribute.color`, `fontWeight`, etc.).
- SSR + DOM-client rendering of attributed runs.
- No `CodeHighlighter` SPI and no `color.code.*` tokens.

## Proposed approach

1. Add a `CodeHighlighter` seam in `pathland-docs`:
   `highlight(code: String, language: String?): AttributedString`.
2. Implement a small built-in tokenizer for the languages the docs use most:
   Kotlin, Java, Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, shell, JSON, HTML/XML, Markdown.
   Unknown languages fall back to plain text.
3. Emit `AttributedString` color/style runs (keyword, string, comment, number,
   type, function, punctuation) while keeping the code text byte-identical.
4. Add semantic design tokens with light/dark values:
   `color.code.background`, `color.code.text`, `color.code.keyword`,
   `color.code.string`, `color.code.comment`, `color.code.number`,
   `color.code.type`, `color.code.function`, `color.code.punctuation`,
   `color.code.added`, `color.code.removed`.
5. Keep SSR self-contained and hydrated output identical; add golden fixtures.
6. Do not introduce a client-side highlighter or raw HTML.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fenced blocks with a supported language render highlighted in SSR and after
  hydration.
- Unknown/absent languages render plain monospace.
- Highlighting never changes the code text (copy/selection remains exact).
- Light and dark color schemes use the code tokens and meet contrast.
- Tests cover each supported language, unknown fallback, and hydration/delta
  stability.
- The highlighter is optional; disabling it returns the v1 plain rendering.

## Non-goals

- Line numbers, copy buttons, and diff views (separate enhancements).
- Client-side JavaScript highlighting.
- Raw HTML injection in Markdown.
```

## Verification unchanged

- v1 code blocks still need the `WHITE_SPACE` protocol property and renderer
  coverage; the issue adds no protocol requirements.
- The docs fixtures should assert monospace, preserved whitespace, language
  label, and horizontal scroll behavior — but not colors.
- No open decisions remain.

No files were changed (plan mode).
