title: Documentation
description: Learn Pathland's opcode protocol, reactive engine, and Kotlin DSL.
section: Start here
order: 0
---

# Pathland documentation

Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol. You describe **what**
the UI is with a retained, declarative view tree; the engine emits a fixed
16-byte opcode stream, and each renderer maps that stream onto its own native
elements.

> Write once, render anywhere — without a canvas and without a WebView.

## What you get

- A **binary protocol**: every instruction is exactly 16 bytes.
- A **diff-based reactive engine**: only changed nodes emit opcodes.
- **Native elements** on every target: GTK4, DOM, Qt Quick, and future hosts.
- A **Kotlin DSL** with SwiftUI-shaped builders, signals, state, routing, and
  media controllers.

## Where to go next

- [Getting started](getting-started.md) — build and run the Quarkus docs demo.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) — opcodes, rings, arenas, and renderers.
- [Kotlin DSL](kotlin-dsl.md) — components, modifiers, state, and routing.
- [Markdown in the docs kit](markdown.md) — what the block renderer supports.

## A first view

```kotlin
VStack(spacing = 12f) {
    Text("Hello, Pathland")
        .font(Font.largeTitle())
    Button("Read the docs") {}
        .buttonStyle(plainButtonStyle())
        .navigate("/docs/getting-started")
}
```

The same `View` tree can be mounted by a Quarkus server, a Spring Boot server,
or a desktop host. The renderer is the only platform-specific part.

# Getting started

## Prerequisites

- JDK 17 or newer
- Maven 3.9+
- (Optional) Rust for the native renderers

## Build the JVM libraries

```bash
cd lib/java
mvn install
```

The JVM path is pure Java/Kotlin: the HTML renderer and the inline Markdown
parser are ports, so no Rust toolchain is required for the server demos.

## Run the docs site

```bash
cd lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080`. The marketing page is at `/` and this
documentation starts at `/docs`.

## How a page is loaded

1. `DocsRepository` reads `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`.
2. Each listed `.md` resource is parsed for front matter and a CommonMark body.
3. `DocsLayout` renders the page, sidebar, TOC, and prev/next links.
4. `Markdown(...)` maps blocks to Kotlin DSL views.
5. The engine emits opcodes; the Quarkus starter renders SSR HTML and then
   keeps the page live over `/_pathland/ws`.

## Front matter

```markdown
---
title: Getting started
description: Build the Java libraries and run the docs site locally.
section: Start here
order: 10
---
```

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `title` | Page heading and navigation label |
| `description` | Head meta description and intro paragraph |
| `section` | Sidebar group |
| `order` | Sort order inside the section |
| `route` | Optional override for the derived route |
| `draft` | Hide the page |

---
title: Architecture
description: The opcode engine, shared ring, arena, and renderer contract.
section: Concepts
order: 20
---

# Architecture

Pathland has four moving parts.

## 1. The application owns the tree

The application builds a retained view tree. Nodes carry properties,
constraints, text, event listeners, and signal bindings. The application owns
all business state.

## 2. The engine emits deltas

The engine compares the new tree with the previous snapshot and emits only the
changes:

```text
TREE      CREATE_NODE / INSERT_CHILD / REMOVE_CHILD / DELETE_NODE / MOVE_CHILD
PARAMETER SET_PROPERTY / SET_TEXT / SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT / SET_DESIGN_TOKEN
META      RESET / ENVIRONMENT / WINDOW_METADATA / RESYNC
EVENT     POINTER_* / KEY_* / TEXT_CHANGED / NAVIGATE / MEDIA_*
```

An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.

## 3. The transport is shared memory or a binary batch

Every opcode is 16 bytes:

```text
[category: u8][command: u8][flags: u16][A: u32][B: u32][C: u32]
```

On desktop, the guest writes into a ring buffer in shared linear memory. Over
the network, the same opcodes travel in a `PLPL` batch with a string section.

## 4. The renderer maps to native elements

Renderers are stateless with respect to the application:

- HTML → flex containers, spans, buttons, native form controls
- GTK4 → `GtkBox`, `GtkLabel`, `GtkButton`, …
- Qt Quick → Row/Column/Text and Qt Quick Controls

Renderers keep only their own rendered output tree — a cache for drawing, hit
testing, and event routing. They never keep application state.

> The engine describes WHAT the UI is, never WHERE it is. It does not compute
> layout and does not emit rects.

---
title: Kotlin DSL
description: Build views, state, routing, and navigation with the Kotlin authoring DSL.
section: Guides
order: 30
---

# Kotlin DSL

The Kotlin DSL is the sole JVM authoring surface. It is shared by Quarkus,
Spring Boot, and desktop hosts.

## Components

```kotlin
VStack(spacing = 12f) {
    Text("Hello")
    HStack(spacing = 8f) {
        Button("Save") { save() }
        Button("Cancel") { cancel() }
    }
}
```

Common builders include `Text`, `Image`, `Button`, `TextField`, `VStack`,
`HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `Spacer`, `Divider`, `Video`, and
`NavigationStack`.

## Modifiers

```kotlin
Text("Pathland")
    .font(Font.title())
    .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
    .foregroundStyle(Color.token("color.primary"))
    .padding(16f)
    .background(Color.token("color.surface"))
    .border(Color.token("color.border"), 1f, 8f)
```

Modifiers are chainable Kotlin values. Design-token references resolve in the
renderer and adapt to light/dark schemes.

## State and signals

```kotlin
class Counter : Component() {
    private var count by state(0)

    override fun body(): View = VStack(spacing = 12f) {
        Text("Count: $count")
        Button("Increment") { count += 1 }
    }
}
```

A signal read in `body()` subscribes the component. A write re-renders only that
component and diffs its retained subtree. A signal bound to a node stays
fine-grained and does not re-run `body()`.

## Routing

```kotlin
val router = navigator("/") {
    route("/", HomeView())
    route("/docs", DocsView())
    fallback(NotFoundView())
}

NavigationStack(router)
```

Navigation intents are resolved by the emitter. Use `navigate` to replace the
current route, or `push`/`pop` for a drill-down stack.

## Markdown pages

The docs kit adds `Markdown(...)`, `DocsLayout`, and `DocsRepository` on top of
the DSL. Markdown is parsed into views — not into HTML.

---
title: Markdown support
description: The blocks the docs kit renders, and how they map to the Kotlin DSL.
section: Guides
order: 40
---

# Markdown support

The docs kit parses Markdown with commonmark-java plus GFM tables. It maps the
AST to Kotlin DSL views; it never renders HTML directly.

## Supported blocks

| Block | DSL mapping |
|---|---|
| Heading | `Text` + heading `Font` + anchor id |
| Paragraph | `Text` with inline runs |
| Bullet list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `•` markers |
| Ordered list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `1.`, `2.`, … |
| Fenced code | monospace `CodeBlock` with preserved whitespace |
| Block quote | accent bar + nested blocks |
| Thematic break | `Divider` |
| Table | `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling |
| Image | `Image` with alt text |
| Inline link | `AttributedString` link run |
| Raw HTML | escaped literal text (never executed) |

## Inline styles

- **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~
- [links](getting-started.md)
- nested emphasis such as **bold with *italic* inside**

## Images

![The rendered browser demo](/docs-assets/screenshot_browser.png)

Relative image paths are prefixed with `MarkdownOptions.imageBase`; absolute
paths and URLs are left unchanged.

## Code blocks

```kotlin
fun greeting(name: String): String = "Hello, $name"
```

Code blocks are monospace in v1. Syntax highlighting is tracked as a follow-up
issue because code is the primary content of a protocol docs site; the
`AttributedString` model and renderers already support color runs.

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/**
 * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
 *
 * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
 *
 * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
 * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
 */
data class Opcode(
    val category: Int,
    val command: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val a: Int,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun category(): Int = category
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun flags(): Int = flags
    fun a(): Int = a
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
        out[0] = category.toByte()
        out[1] = command.toByte()
        out[2] = flags.toByte()
        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
        return out
    }

    companion object {
        const val SIZE = 16

        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
            return Opcode(
                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
            )
        }

        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
            out[offset] = value.toByte()
            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
        }

        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
    }
}

`ALIGNMENT` **positions** children in the leftover cross-axis space; it never
  resizes them. The cross-axis default is *hug* (children keep their size;
  only `FILL`-sized children stretch). Full contract: [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).
- **`CONTENT_MODE` enum**: `Fit`=0 (aspect-fit within the bounds),
  `Fill`=1 (aspect-fill, cropped).
- **`OFFSET`** moves the element **after** layout without affecting layout
  (post-layout translation).
- **`POSITION`** is absolute placement within the parent; the renderer resolves
  the anchor.

## 2. Text Formatting

Apply to `Text`, `Label`, `Button` labels, and text-bearing controls. Renderers
map them to their native text attributes.

The same property vocabulary scopes to character ranges in
`PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` style runs. V1 run attributes are `FONT_SIZE`,
`FONT_WEIGHT`, `COLOR`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`, and
`STRIKETHROUGH`; `FONT_FAMILY` (a `STRING`) and the remaining line/effect
properties stay node-level only. See
[OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#attributed-text-payload-set_attributed_text).

cat > /tmp/pathland-syntax-issue.md <<'EOF'
## Context

The Pathland docs site renders Markdown fenced code blocks through the Kotlin DSL. v1 deliberately ships **plain monospace code blocks** with preserved whitespace (`WHITE_SPACE = PRE`), horizontal scrolling, and an optional language label. This keeps the initial docs implementation small and avoids adding a highlighter before the content pipeline is proven.

Code samples are central to Pathland's documentation: the protocol, opcode layout, DSL usage, and every renderer/host example are expressed as code. Plain monospace is readable, but it does not help readers scan a snippet or distinguish keywords, strings, comments, types, and function names.

## Why this is needed

- **Comprehension:** highlighting makes structure visible at a glance, which matters for a protocol with compact binary layouts and multiple language bindings (Kotlin, Java, Rust, TypeScript, shell).
- **Error spotting:** color distinguishes strings from identifiers and comments, so malformed examples are easier to notice.
- **Cross-language comparison:** the same docs show Kotlin/Java/Rust/TS versions of the same API; consistent highlighting helps readers map concepts.
- **Docs quality:** highlighted code is a baseline expectation for developer documentation and makes the site feel finished.
- **Accessibility and theming:** semantic code tokens can be tuned for contrast in both light and dark schemes, instead of using ad-hoc literal colors.
- **No protocol gap:** `AttributedString` already supports color/style runs and every renderer already maps those runs to spans/CSS. The missing piece is the highlighter and design tokens, not new wire capability.

## What v1 has

- `CodeBlock` with monospace text, preserved whitespace, padding/background/border, horizontal scroll, and a language label.
- `AttributedString` style runs (`TextAttribute.color`, `fontWeight`, etc.).
- SSR + DOM-client rendering of attributed runs.
- No `CodeHighlighter` SPI and no `color.code.*` tokens.

## Proposed approach

1. Add a `CodeHighlighter` seam in `pathland-docs`:
   `highlight(code: String, language: String?): AttributedString`.
2. Implement a small built-in tokenizer for the languages the docs use most:
   Kotlin, Java, Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, shell, JSON, HTML/XML, Markdown.
   Unknown languages fall back to plain text.
3. Emit `AttributedString` color/style runs (keyword, string, comment, number,
   type, function, punctuation) while keeping the code text byte-identical.
4. Add semantic design tokens with light/dark values:
   `color.code.background`, `color.code.text`, `color.code.keyword`,
   `color.code.string`, `color.code.comment`, `color.code.number`,
   `color.code.type`, `color.code.function`, `color.code.punctuation`,
   `color.code.added`, `color.code.removed`.
5. Keep SSR self-contained and hydrated output identical; add golden fixtures.
6. Do not introduce a client-side highlighter or raw HTML.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fenced blocks with a supported language render highlighted in SSR and after hydration.
- Unknown/absent languages render plain monospace.
- Highlighting never changes the code text (copy/selection remains exact).
- Light and dark color schemes use the code tokens and meet contrast.
- Tests cover each supported language, unknown fallback, and hydration/delta stability.
- The highlighter is optional; disabling it returns the v1 plain rendering.

## Non-goals

- Line numbers, copy buttons, and diff views (separate enhancements).
- Client-side JavaScript highlighting.
- Raw HTML injection in Markdown.
EOF

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`,
  `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.
- **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin
  model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and
  payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal<AttributedString>)`
  emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks.
- **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the v1 subset by default
  (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``,
  `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`); `markdown = false` renders literal text.
  `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now a **pure-Java parser** (no native
  library, so it runs on every platform and under GraalVM native-image); it is a
  behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-markdown` crate (pre-scan + bounded
  cache). The Rust crate remains the parser for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts.
  Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path; rich results emit
  `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive `Text(Signal<String>)` parses on change.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
  `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
  during a component render.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
  `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
  bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
  annotation processor are removed.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
  **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled
  `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them
  against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are
  bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). A declared `opcodeCount` that overflows
  `Int` arithmetic now throws instead of triggering an OOM allocation.

# pathland-docs — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The reusable Kotlin docs kit: CommonMark/GFM block parsing into Pathland views,
code blocks, tables, a `.md` resource repository, and a docs page shell. It emits
**views**, never HTML — the renderers remain the only HTML producers.

## Implemented

- **Block Markdown** (`Markdown(...)`, CommonMark + GFM tables/strikethrough):
  headings (with `ANCHOR` ids), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/nested lists, task
  list markers, fenced/indented code blocks, block quotes, thematic breaks,
  GFM tables, block images, inline links, and raw-HTML-as-literal-text.
- **Inline rendering** into `AttributedString` (bold/italic/code/strikethrough/
  links; images become alt text), with a `linkResolver` hook and `imageBase`
  prefix.
- **`CodeBlock`**: monospace, `WHITE_SPACE = PRE`, optional language label,
  padding/background/border, horizontal scroll. **No syntax highlighting** (see
  issue #188; deferred deliberately).
- **Tables**: `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling and per-cell alignment.
  Visual only — semantic table roles are deferred with the protocol work.
- **TOC**: `MarkdownHeadings.extract` + `Slugger` (duplicate-safe ids).
- **`DocsPage.fromMarkdown`**: flat front matter (`title`, `description`,
  `section`, `order`, `route`, `draft`, `updated`, `image`), route derivation,
  and a `DocsRepository` that loads an index + classpath resources or a
  filesystem directory.
- **`DocsLayout`**: header, sidebar, content, TOC, prev/next, per-page
  `windowMetadata`.
- **Tests**: `MarkdownViewTest` covers headings/anchors, lists/images, code
  whitespace, GFM tables, front matter/routes, slug dedupe, and raw HTML.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Syntax highlighting (issue #188).
- Semantic table roles (deferred; tables are visual grids for now).
- Inline images inside a paragraph (rendered as alt text; block images only).
- Footnotes, GFM alerts/admonitions, and autolinks beyond CommonMark.
- A build-time docs index generator (the demo ships a hand-maintained
  `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`; `DocsRepository.fromDirectory` covers dev/tests).
EOF

Notes:
- The web demos need a JDK 17+ (the whole stack runs on every LTS from 17).
- The GTK demos need the GTK4 + libadwaita system libraries.
- On macOS the Java GTK demo hands GTK the main thread automatically
  (`-XstartOnFirstThread`); Linux needs nothing special.

The same commands without the scripts:

```bash
# one-time: build the Java reactor (pure JVM — no Rust/native build needed)
cd lib/java && mvn install

# Spring Boot demo
cd lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo
mvn -q package && java -jar target/pathland-spring-boot-demo-0.1.0.jar
# → http://localhost:8080

# Quarkus Java demo (dev mode with hot reload)
cd lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
# → http://localhost:8080

# Same protocol, native GTK desktop renderer (no browser)
cd lib/rust && cargo run -p pathland-render-gtk-demo

# Same protocol via Kotlin: the shared MusicPlayerView under the GTK renderer
cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk
cd lib/java/pathland-desktop-demo
MAVEN_OPTS="-XstartOnFirstThread" mvn -q compile exec:java \
  -Dpathland.core.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_core.dylib \
  -Dpathland.gtk.lib=$PWD/../../lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_gtk.dylib
# (macOS needs -XstartOnFirstThread; Linux can drop it)
```

Implemented on branch `feat/docs-site` (uncommitted).

- Added CommonMark/GFM block Markdown rendering via the new `pathland-docs` Kotlin module; `Text` now reuses commonmark-java in an inline-only mode.
- Added `WHITE_SPACE` and `ANCHOR` protocol properties across Rust, Java, TypeScript, renderers, specs, manifest, and golden fixtures.
- Added `pathland-docs-demo`: marketing page at `/`, docs at `/docs`, `.md` content, sidebar/TOC, relative-link routing, per-page SEO metadata, and generated sitemap entries.
- Code blocks are monospace only. Filed syntax highlighting follow-up: https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/188
- Verified with `mvn install`, `cargo test`, `npm test` (296 tests), and SSR smoke tests for all pages/assets/sitemap.

Run it with:

```bash
cd lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
```

Remaining known gaps are tracked in `pathland-docs/status.md`: semantic table roles, search, syntax highlighting, and a build-time docs index generator.

/** The Kotlin-authored Pathland marketing + docs app. */
class DocsSite : PathlandApp {

    private val repository: DocsRepository = DocsRepository.fromResources()

    override fun newRoot(): View = DocsRoot(repository)

    override fun sitemapRoutes(): List<String> = listOf("/") + repository.routes()

    override fun pageMetadata(request: PageMetadataRequest): PageMetadata {
        val route = request.route()
        val page = repository.page(route)
        return if (page != null) {
            PageMetadata.builder()
                .title("${page.title} · Pathland")
                .description(page.description)
                .ogType("article")
                .imageUrl(page.image)
                .build()
        } else {
            PageMetadata.builder()
                .title("Pathland — the declarative UI protocol")
                .description(
                    "Write UI once in Kotlin, Rust, or any host; emit a 16-byte " +
                        "opcode stream and render native elements everywhere.",
                )
                .ogType("website")
                .build()
        }
    }
}

private class MarketingPage(private val docsHome: String) : View {
    override fun renderNode(env: dev.pathland.view.core.Environment): dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode =
        page().renderNode(env)

    private fun page(): View = VStack(spacing = 0f) {
        Header(docsHome)
        VStack(spacing = 24f) {
            HStack(alignment = VerticalAlignment.CENTER, spacing = 40f) {
                VStack(alignment = HorizontalAlignment.LEADING, spacing = 16f) {
                    Text("Write UI once.")
                        .font(Font.largeTitle())
                        .fontWeight(FontWeight.BOLD)
                    Text("Render it everywhere.")
            .border(Color.token("color.border"), 1f, 8f)
            .navigate(route)
    }
}

private class NotFoundPage : View {
    override fun renderNode(env: dev.pathland.view.core.Environment): dev.pathland.view.engine.PathlandNode =
        VStack(spacing = 16f) {
            Text("Not found").font(Font.largeTitle())
            Text("That page does not exist.")
            Button("Back to the docs") {}.buttonStyle(plainButtonStyle()).navigate("/docs")
        }.padding(40f).renderNode(env)
}


/** The per-session root: binds the router to the host's active-path signal. */
private class DocsRoot(private val repository: DocsRepository) : View {
    private var router: Router? = null

    override fun renderNode(env: Environment): PathlandNode {
        val pages = repository.pages
        val docsHome = pages.first().route
        val activePath = Environment.value(Platform.ACTIVE_PATH)
        val resolved = router ?: navigator(activePath) {
            route("/", MarketingPage(docsHome))
            for (page in pages) {
                route(page.route, DocsLayout(page, repository))
            }
            fallback(NotFoundPage())
        }.also { router = it }
        return NavigationStack(resolved).renderNode(env)
    }
}

content.text:
Implemented the expanded site on `feat/docs-site` (uncommitted).

- Landing page now includes a **live signal-bound playground** (counter + text field) plus a component-reference CTA.
- Added a SwiftUI-docs-style component reference at `/docs/components`:
  - summary, overview, live preview, declaration, examples, parameter table, availability badges, notes, and see-also links
  - one page each for Text, Image, Icon, Color, Shape, Divider, Spacer, ProgressView, Gauge, Video, VStack, HStack, ZStack, Grid, ScrollView, lazy stacks/grids, GridRow, ViewThatFits, Button, TextField, TextEditor, Toggle, Slider, Stepper, DatePicker, Picker, Menu, ColorPicker, Label, MediaController, ForEach, and Comment
- Added reusable `ComponentDoc` / `ComponentDocsPage` / `ComponentDocsIndexPage` to `pathland-docs`.
- Verified every sitemap route returns `200` (42 routes) and `pathland-docs` tests pass.

Run:

```bash
cd lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080` and `http://localhost:8080/docs/components`.

Each docs page should be a seperate markdown file. In each, it should be possible to add a code example of how to use the said element(component, modifier etc) and the page should also show the example live.

# Plan: Markdown-per-page docs with live examples

## Core design

Every docs page becomes its own `.md` file. A fenced code block can opt into a live preview with an id:

````markdown
```kotlin live=text-basic
Text("Hello, Pathland")
    .font(Font.title())
```
````

The Markdown renderer:

1. parses the fence info string (`kotlin live=text-basic`),
2. renders the code block with language `kotlin`,
3. looks up `text-basic` in a Kotlin `LiveExamples` registry,
4. renders the registered view directly below the code in a bordered “Live preview” card.

The snippet remains the displayed documentation; the registry supplies the executable view. Runtime Kotlin compilation of the snippet is not recommended — it adds a compiler dependency, startup cost, native-image problems, and arbitrary-code risk. A test will enforce that every `live=` id has a registry entry, and every registry entry is used.

## Content structure

Move the current generated component pages into real Markdown resources:

```
docs/components/index.md
docs/components/text.md
docs/components/image.md
docs/components/button.md
...
docs/modifiers/index.md
docs/modifiers/padding.md
docs/modifiers/frame.md
docs/modifiers/background.md
...
```

Each component page uses the existing front matter and a consistent SwiftUI-docs-style body:

```markdown
---
title: Text
description: Displays styled, attributed text — including inline Markdown.
section: Components
order: 100
---

# Text

Displays styled, attributed text.

## Overview
...

## Live example
```kotlin live=text-basic
Text("Hello, Pathland").font(Font.title())
```

## Declaration
```kotlin
fun Text(text: String, markdown: Boolean = true): View
```

## Parameters
| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `String` | The text content |
...

## Availability
Web · GTK · Qt

## See Also
- [Icon](icon.md)
```

The component and modifier index pages are also `.md` files containing link tables/lists.

## Code changes

### `pathland-docs`

- `MarkdownOptions` gains:
  ```kotlin
  val liveExamples: Map<String, () -> View> = emptyMap()
  ```
- `MarkdownView.kt` `FencedCodeBlock` handling:
  - parse the info string (`language`, `live=<id>`),
  - if a registered view exists, render `CodeBlock(...)` + a `LivePreviewCard(view)`,
  - if the id is missing/unknown, render the code block alone (the docs test catches missing ids).
- Add a small reusable `LivePreviewCard` helper.
- `DocsLayout` accepts `liveExamples` and passes it into `MarkdownOptions` for every markdown page.
- Remove the generated `ComponentDocsPage` / `ComponentDocsIndexPage` path and its `tocOverride`/`content` parameters once all pages are Markdown. Keep `DocsLayout` focused on markdown.
- If preferred, keep `ComponentDocs.kt` only for a shared preview-card helper; otherwise delete it.

### `pathland-docs-demo`

- Delete the `PathlandComponents.kt` catalog as the source of documentation.
- Add `LiveExamples.kt`:
  ```kotlin
  object LiveExamples {
      val byId: Map<String, () -> View> = mapOf(
          "text-basic" to { Text("Hello, Pathland").font(Font.title()) },
          "button-counter" to { CounterDemo() },
          ...
      )
  }
  ```
  - Move the existing interactive demo components (`CounterDemo`, `TextFieldDemo`, `ToggleDemo`, etc.) here.
  - Use unique state keys per example id.
- `DocsSite` passes `liveExamples = LiveExamples.byId` to `DocsLayout`; all docs pages use the normal markdown route. No component catalog or special router branch.
- Generate `META-INF/pathland-docs.index` at build time from `target/classes/docs/**/*.md` (Maven Ant `pathconvert` or a small exec/indexer). Remove the hand-maintained index file.
- Keep `/docs/components` and add `/docs/modifiers` to the landing-page CTA/navigation.
- Update `pathland-docs` and `pathland-docs-demo` `status.md`.

## Modifiers coverage

Add a `Modifiers` section for the most important DSL modifiers, each with a live example:

- padding
- frame
- background
- border / cornerRadius
- shadow
- font / fontSize / fontWeight
- foregroundStyle
- lineLimit
- opacity
- whiteSpace
- anchor
- disabled
- accessibilityLabel
- onTapGesture

Each is its own `.md` file with the same structure: overview, live example, declaration, notes, availability, see-also.

## Tests and verification

- `MarkdownViewTest`:
  - `live=` fence renders both the code block and the registered preview,
  - unknown `live=` id falls back to code-only,
  - no registry entries are required for ordinary code fences.
- Docs-demo test:
  - load every `.md` page from the generated repository,
  - assert every `live=<id>` has a `LiveExamples.byId` entry,
  - optionally assert every registry id is referenced,
  - assert every page route resolves.
- Verify all component/modifier routes return `200`; check live interactive demos SSR correctly.
- Run `mvn -q -pl pathland-docs -am test`, `mvn -q -pl pathland-docs-demo -am package`, and the existing Rust/TS tests.

## Open questions

1. **Modifier scope**: start with the core set above (recommended), or create a page for every modifier in the DSL?
2. **Index generation**: generate the docs index at build time (recommended), or keep a hand-maintained `pathland-docs.index`?

        The pure-Java HTML renderer (dev.pathland.render.html): a behavioural port
        of the Rust pathland-render-html crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
        self-contained snapshot frame and renders it to HTML in one pass. No native
        library is loaded, so it runs on every platform and is GraalVM native-image
        compatible. The server-side/remote-projection target, usable from Spring
        Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>test-compile</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- The generated base design is owned by design/ and synced into the
                 Rust renderer's assets by scripts/sync-design-css.sh. Embed those
                 committed bytes as classpath resources for the Java port. -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-resources-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>copy-base-css</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>copy-resources</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <outputDirectory>${project.build.outputDirectory}/dev/pathland/render/html</outputDirectory>
                            <resources>
                                <resource>
                                    <directory>${project.basedir}/../../rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets</directory>
                                    <includes>
                                        <include>base.css</include>
                                        <include>base.css.name</include>
                                    </includes>
                                </resource>
                            </resources>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# Plan: one Markdown file per docs page + live examples

Decisions locked: **core modifier set** and **build-time index generation**.

## 1. Live-example mechanism

A Markdown page can mark a Kotlin fence as live:

````markdown
```kotlin live=text-basic
Text("Hello, Pathland")
    .font(Font.title())
```
````

Rendering rules:

- Parse the fence info string into `language = kotlin` and `liveId = text-basic`.
- Render the normal code block immediately followed by a bordered **LIVE PREVIEW** card.
- Resolve `liveId` from a Kotlin registry: `Map<String, () -> View>`.
- If the id is missing/unknown, render the code block only; tests fail on unregistered ids.
- The Markdown snippet remains the displayed source. The registry supplies the compiled `View`; runtime Kotlin compilation is deliberately avoided.

Implementation points:

- `MarkdownOptions` gains `liveExamples: Map<String, () -> View>`.
- `MarkdownView.kt` `FencedCodeBlock` branch parses `live=<id>` and emits `CodeBlock(...)` + the preview card.
- `DocsLayout` accepts `liveExamples` and forwards it to `MarkdownOptions`.
- The live view is constructed inside the preview card’s scope, so interactive `Component` demos bind to session state correctly.

## 2. Move all docs content to Markdown

### Components

Create one file per component under:

```
lib/java/pathland-docs-demo/src/main/resources/docs/components/
  index.md
  text.md
  image.md
  icon.md
  color.md
  shape.md
  divider.md
  spacer.md
  progress-view.md
  gauge.md
  video.md
  vstack.md
  hstack.md
  zstack.md
  grid.md
  scroll-view.md
  lazy-vstack.md
  lazy-hstack.md
  lazy-vgrid.md
  lazy-hgrid.md
  grid-row.md
  view-that-fits.md
  button.md
  text-field.md
  text-editor.md
  toggle.md
  slider.md
  stepper.md
  date-picker.md
  picker.md
  menu.md
  color-picker.md
  label.md
  media-controller.md
  for-each.md
  comment.md
```

Each page uses the same structure:

```markdown
---
title: Text
description: Displays styled, attributed text.
section: Components
order: 100
---

# Text

Short summary.

## Overview
...

## Live example
```kotlin live=text-basic
Text("Hello, Pathland").font(Font.title())
```

## Declaration
```kotlin
fun Text(text: String, markdown: Boolean = true): View
```

## Parameters
| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `String` | The text content |

## Availability
Web · GTK · Qt

## See Also
- [Icon](icon.md)
```

`components/index.md` is a Markdown table/list linking every component page.

### Modifiers (core set)

Create `docs/modifiers/`:

```
index.md
padding.md
frame.md
background.md
border.md
corner-radius.md
shadow.md
font.md
foreground-style.md
line-limit.md
opacity.md
white-space.md
anchor.md
disabled.md
accessibility-label.md
on-tap-gesture.md
```

Each modifier page has the same structure and a live example, e.g.:

```markdown
## Live example
```kotlin live=modifier-padding
Text("Padded")
    .padding(16f)
    .background(Color.token("color.surface"))
```
```

Pages with no meaningful visual preview (`Comment`, and `ProxyView`/`MediaController` where a live dependency is not practical) remain code-only; the live mechanism is available on every Markdown page.

## 3. Live example registry

Add:

```
lib/java/pathland-docs-demo/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/demo/docs/LiveExamples.kt
```

```kotlin
object LiveExamples {
    val byId: Map<String, () -> View> = mapOf(
        "text-basic" to { Text("Hello, Pathland").font(Font.title()) },
        "button-counter" to { CounterDemo() },
        "text-field" to { TextFieldDemo() },
        "modifier-padding" to {
            Text("Padded")
                .padding(16f)
                .background(Color.token("color.surface"))
        },
        // ...
    )
}
```

- Move the existing interactive demo components (`CounterDemo`, `TextFieldDemo`, `ToggleDemo`, `SliderDemo`, etc.) into this file.
- Use unique state keys per example id.
- Add every `live=<id>` used in Markdown.
- Add a test that every `live=` id in every loaded docs page exists in `byId`.

## 4. Remove the generated Kotlin catalog

- Delete `PathlandComponents.kt`.
- Delete `ComponentDocs.kt` (or keep only a shared preview-card helper if useful).
- Remove the special component-page router branch from `DocsSite`.
- All docs pages, including component/modifier indexes, go through the normal `DocsLayout` + Markdown route.
- Remove `DocsLayout`’s `tocOverride`/`content` parameters if they become unused.
- Keep the landing page as Kotlin DSL; add a “Modifiers” CTA/link next to “Components.”

## 5. Generate the docs index at build time

Remove the hand-maintained `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`.

Add a Maven step to `pathland-docs-demo/pom.xml` (Ant `fileset` + `pathconvert` + `echo`) that:

1. scans `src/main/resources/docs/**/*.md`,
2. writes `target/classes/META-INF/pathland-docs.index` with one classpath path per line.

This keeps `DocsRepository.fromResources()` unchanged and works for Quarkus dev, packaged jars, and tests. The index is regenerated on every Maven build.

If desired, add a small test that every `.md` file under `src/main/resources/docs` appears in the generated index.

## 6. Tests and verification

- `MarkdownViewTest`:
  - live fence renders code + registered preview,
  - unknown live id falls back to code-only,
  - ordinary fences are unchanged.
- Docs-demo test:
  - every `live=` id has a registry entry,
  - every docs page route loads,
  - generated index covers every `.md` file.
- Smoke-check every sitemap route returns `200`; verify live previews render in SSR.
- Run:
  - `mvn -q -pl pathland-docs -am test`
  - `mvn -q -pl pathland-docs-demo -am package`
  - existing Rust/TS suites if protocol files are untouched (they should be).
- Update `pathland-docs/status.md`, `pathland-docs-demo/status.md`, and any module list references.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every documentation page is a separate `.md` file.
- Any Markdown page can include ` ```kotlin live=<id> ` and renders the code plus a live preview directly beneath it.
- Component and modifier indexes are Markdown pages.
- The docs index is generated automatically during Maven builds.
- No Kotlin catalog duplicates the Markdown documentation.
- All live ids are registered and covered by tests.

## Objective
- Build a Pathland marketing site plus documentation site using the **Kotlin DSL**, with docs authored as separate `.md` files, SwiftUI-style component/modifier pages, and **live previews of code examples**.
- Latest request: each docs page must be its own Markdown file and support a code example that also renders live.

## Important Details
- Repository: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland`.
- Branch: `feat/docs-site`. Commit already created: `9a86b9bf feat(docs): add Kotlin Markdown documentation site`.
- There is a second wave of **uncommitted** work adding the expanded landing page and component catalog:
  - modified `DocsSite.kt`, `docs/index.md`, `DocsLayout.kt`, `DocsRepository.kt`, status files
  - untracked `PathlandComponents.kt`, `ComponentDocs.kt`
- User constraints/decisions:
  - Docs content must be `.md` resources, not Kotlin catalog-generated pages.
  - Authoring/rendering must remain via Kotlin DSL; no Markdown-to-HTML shortcut.
  - Use `commonmark-java` 0.24.0 + GFM tables.
  - `WHITE_SPACE` and `ANCHOR` protocol properties were approved.
  - Table protocol roles deferred; tables are visual grids.
  - Search deferred.
  - Code blocks are plain monospace only; syntax highlighting tracked in issue #188: `https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/188`
- Latest proposed live-example mechanism:
  - Markdown fence syntax: ` ```kotlin live=text-basic `
  - Renderer shows the code block, then looks up `text-basic` in a Kotlin `LiveExamples.byId` registry and renders the registered view below it.
  - Do **not** compile/execute Markdown snippets at runtime.
  - Add a test enforcing every `live=<id>` has a registry entry.
- Component/modifier docs pages should follow a consistent SwiftUI-docs style: overview, live example, declaration, parameters table, availability, see-also.
- Build-time docs index generation is recommended over the current hand-maintained `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `feat/docs-site` branch.
- Added `WHITE_SPACE` (`0x0022`) and `ANCHOR` (`0x201C`) across Rust constants, Java/TS constants, Rust/Java/TS renderers, specs, manifest, and tests.
- Added `pathland-docs` module:
  - CommonMark/GFM block renderer to Kotlin DSL views
  - `Markdown(...)`, `CodeBlock`, `DocsPage`, `DocsRepository`, `DocsLayout`, TOC/slugger
  - relative `.md` link resolution; docs tests
- Added `pathland-docs-demo` Quarkus app:
  - marketing page at `/`
  - docs at `/docs`
  - `.md` content: `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `architecture.md`, `kotlin-dsl.md`, `markdown.md`
  - sidebar/TOC/prev-next, per-page SEO metadata, sitemap routes
  - docs assets served from `/docs-assets/`
- Expanded landing page with live signal-bound playground and component-reference CTA.
- Added SwiftUI-style `/docs/components` catalog and per-component pages in uncommitted work.
- Created issue #188 for syntax highlighting.
- Verified previously: `mvn install`, `cargo test`, `npm test` (296 tests), all 42 sitemap routes returned `200`.
- `pathland-docs` tests pass after latest uncommitted changes; `pathland-docs-demo` builds.

### Active
- Latest request is **planned but not implemented**: convert all docs pages to separate `.md` files and support live code examples.
- Current uncommitted component docs are Kotlin-catalog-generated (`PathlandComponents.kt` / `ComponentDocs.kt`), which conflicts with the new requirement.
- Need to refactor:
  - Markdown renderer to support `live=<id>` fences
  - add `MarkdownOptions.liveExamples`
  - create `.md` files for components/modifiers
  - add `LiveExamples.kt`
  - remove/replace the Kotlin component catalog
  - generate docs index at build time

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the latest plan: add `live=<id>` fenced-code support to `MarkdownView.kt` via `MarkdownOptions.liveExamples`, then create `LiveExamples.kt` in the demo.
2. Convert `PathlandComponents.kt` content into separate `docs/components/*.md` files plus `docs/components/index.md`; delete the Kotlin catalog and generated component-page path.
3. Add `docs/modifiers/*.md` for the core modifier set, generate `META-INF/pathland-docs.index` at build time, add live-id coverage tests, and re-run smoke tests.

# Pathland documentation

Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol. You describe **what**
the UI is with a retained, declarative view tree; the engine emits a fixed
16-byte opcode stream, and each renderer maps that stream onto its own native
elements.

> Write once, render anywhere — without a canvas and without a WebView.

## What you get

- A **binary protocol**: every instruction is exactly 16 bytes.
- A **diff-based reactive engine**: only changed nodes emit opcodes.
- **Native elements** on every target: GTK4, DOM, Qt Quick, and future hosts.
- A **Kotlin DSL** with SwiftUI-shaped builders, signals, state, routing, and
  media controllers.

## Where to go next

- [Component reference](components) — SwiftUI-style pages with live previews.
- [Getting started](getting-started.md) — build and run the Quarkus docs demo.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) — opcodes, rings, arenas, and renderers.
- [Kotlin DSL](kotlin-dsl.md) — components, modifiers, state, and routing.
- [Markdown in the docs kit](markdown.md) — what the block renderer supports.

## A first view

```kotlin
VStack(spacing = 12f) {
    Text("Hello, Pathland")
        .font(Font.largeTitle())
    Button("Read the docs") {}
        .buttonStyle(plainButtonStyle())
        .navigate("/docs/getting-started")
}
```

The same `View` tree can be mounted by a Quarkus server, a Spring Boot server,
or a desktop host. The renderer is the only platform-specific part.

# Getting started

## Prerequisites

- JDK 17 or newer
- Maven 3.9+
- (Optional) Rust for the native renderers

## Build the JVM libraries

```bash
cd lib/java
mvn install
```

The JVM path is pure Java/Kotlin: the HTML renderer and the inline Markdown
parser are ports, so no Rust toolchain is required for the server demos.

## Run the docs site

```bash
cd lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
mvn quarkus:dev
```

Open `http://localhost:8080`. The marketing page is at `/` and this
documentation starts at `/docs`.

## How a page is loaded

1. `DocsRepository` reads `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`.
2. Each listed `.md` resource is parsed for front matter and a CommonMark body.
3. `DocsLayout` renders the page, sidebar, TOC, and prev/next links.
4. `Markdown(...)` maps blocks to Kotlin DSL views.
5. The engine emits opcodes; the Quarkus starter renders SSR HTML and then
   keeps the page live over `/_pathland/ws`.

            entries.append((slug, body))

    out.append('        },')

out.append('}')
out.append('')
out.append(classes)

# Pathland documentation

Pathland is a cross-platform, cross-language UI protocol. You describe **what**
the UI is with a retained, declarative view tree; the engine emits a fixed
16-byte opcode stream, and each renderer maps that stream onto its own native
elements.

> Write once, render anywhere — without a canvas and without a WebView.

## What you get

- A **binary protocol**: every instruction is exactly 16 bytes.
- A **diff-based reactive engine**: only changed nodes emit opcodes.
- **Native elements** on every target: GTK4, DOM, Qt Quick, and future hosts.
- A **Kotlin DSL** with SwiftUI-shaped builders, signals, state, routing, and
  media controllers.

## Where to go next

- [Component reference](components) — SwiftUI-style pages with live previews.
- [Getting started](getting-started.md) — build and run the Quarkus docs demo.
- [Architecture](architecture.md) — opcodes, rings, arenas, and renderers.
- [Kotlin DSL](kotlin-dsl.md) — components, modifiers, state, and routing.
- [Markdown in the docs kit](markdown.md) — what the block renderer supports.

## A first view

```kotlin
VStack(spacing = 12f) {
    Text("Hello, Pathland")
        .font(Font.largeTitle())
    Button("Read the docs") {}
        .buttonStyle(plainButtonStyle())
        .navigate("/docs/getting-started")
}
```

The same `View` tree can be mounted by a Quarkus server, a Spring Boot server,
or a desktop host. The renderer is the only platform-specific part.

# pathland-docs — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The reusable Kotlin docs kit: CommonMark/GFM block parsing into Pathland views,
code blocks, tables, a `.md` resource repository, and a docs page shell. It emits
**views**, never HTML — the renderers remain the only HTML producers.

## Implemented

- **Block Markdown** (`Markdown(...)`, CommonMark + GFM tables/strikethrough):
  headings (with `ANCHOR` ids), paragraphs, bullet/ordered/nested lists, task
  list markers, fenced/indented code blocks, block quotes, thematic breaks,
  GFM tables, block images, inline links, and raw-HTML-as-literal-text.
- **Inline rendering** into `AttributedString` (bold/italic/code/strikethrough/
  links; images become alt text), with a `linkResolver` hook and `imageBase`
  prefix.
- **`CodeBlock`**: monospace, `WHITE_SPACE = PRE`, optional language label,
  padding/background/border, horizontal scroll. **No syntax highlighting** (see
  issue #188; deferred deliberately).
- **Tables**: `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling and per-cell alignment.
  Visual only — semantic table roles are deferred with the protocol work.
- **TOC**: `MarkdownHeadings.extract` + `Slugger` (duplicate-safe ids).
- **Link resolution**: `DocsRepository.resolveLink` maps relative `.md` targets
  (including fragments/queries) to the target page's route; absolute URLs and
  fragments pass through.
- **`DocsPage.fromMarkdown`**: flat front matter (`title`, `description`,
  `section`, `order`, `route`, `draft`, `updated`, `image`), route derivation,
  and a `DocsRepository` that loads an index + classpath resources or a
  filesystem directory.
- **`DocsLayout`**: header, sidebar, content, TOC, prev/next, per-page
  `windowMetadata`, plus optional `tocOverride`/content lambdas for structured
  (non-Markdown) pages.
- **SwiftUI-style component docs**: `ComponentDoc` + `ComponentDocsPage` render
  summary, overview, live preview, declaration, examples, parameter table,
  availability badges, notes, and see-also links. `ComponentDocsIndexPage` is a
  card grid over the catalog.
- **Tests**: `MarkdownViewTest` covers headings/anchors, lists/images, code
  whitespace, GFM tables, front matter/routes, slug dedupe, and raw HTML.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Syntax highlighting (issue #188).
- Semantic table roles (deferred; tables are visual grids for now).
- Inline images inside a paragraph (rendered as alt text; block images only).
- Footnotes, GFM alerts/admonitions, and autolinks beyond CommonMark.
- A build-time docs index generator (the demo ships a hand-maintained
  `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`; `DocsRepository.fromDirectory` covers dev/tests).

# Markdown support

The docs kit parses Markdown with commonmark-java plus GFM tables. It maps the
AST to Kotlin DSL views; it never renders HTML directly.

## Supported blocks

| Block | DSL mapping |
|---|---|
| Heading | `Text` + heading `Font` + anchor id |
| Paragraph | `Text` with inline runs |
| Bullet list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `•` markers |
| Ordered list | nested `VStack`/`HStack` with `1.`, `2.`, … |
| Fenced code | monospace `CodeBlock` with preserved whitespace |
| Block quote | accent bar + nested blocks |
| Thematic break | `Divider` |
| Table | `Grid`/`GridRow` with header styling |
| Image | `Image` with alt text |
| Inline link | `AttributedString` link run |
| Raw HTML | escaped literal text (never executed) |

## Inline styles

- **bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~strikethrough~~
- [links](getting-started.md)
- nested emphasis such as **bold with *italic* inside**

## Images

![The rendered browser demo](/docs-assets/screenshot_browser.png)

Relative image paths are prefixed with `MarkdownOptions.imageBase`; absolute
paths and URLs are left unchanged.

## Code blocks

```kotlin
fun greeting(name: String): String = "Hello, $name"
```

Code blocks are monospace in v1. Syntax highlighting is tracked as
[issue #188](https://github.com/PathlandDev/Pathland/issues/188) because code is
the primary content of a protocol docs site; the `AttributedString` model and
renderers already support color runs.

# Text

Displays styled, attributed text — including inline Markdown.

## Overview

Text is the primary content primitive. Inline Markdown is parsed into style runs by default; pass `markdown = false` for literal text. Typos and code spans become `AttributedString` runs, while a plain result keeps the compact `SET_TEXT` path.

## Declaration

```kotlin
fun Text(text: String, markdown: Boolean = true): View
```

## Examples

### Inline Markdown

Bold, italic, code, strikethrough, and links are parsed into attributed runs.

```kotlin
Text("A **bold** and *italic* line with `code`.")
```

### Styled heading

A heading text style is rendered as a semantic heading.

```kotlin
Text("Getting started").font(Font.largeTitle())
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `TEXT` | `String` | The text content |
| `TEXT_STYLE` | `TextStyle` | Predefined typography; heading styles imply h1–h5 |
| `FONT_SIZE` | `Float` | Explicit point size |
| `FONT_WEIGHT` | `FontWeight` | Regular, medium, semibold, bold |
| `FONT_DESIGN` | `FontDesign` | Default, serif, rounded, monospaced |
| `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | `TextAlignment` | Leading, center, trailing |
| `LINE_LIMIT` | `Int` | Maximum rendered lines |

## Availability

Web · GTK · Qt

- [Icon](icon.md)
- [Label](label.md)
- [Image](image.md)

### Sequence gap detection

The network backend is reliable and ordered **within a connection**, but a
middlebox can drop a batch while the socket stays "open", and a producer's send
path can wedge — either way the consumer silently misses deltas. The batch
`sequence` makes that loss detectable:

- **Producer**: maintain one monotonic `sequence` per stream, incremented by
  exactly one for **each encoded batch**. Only guest → host delta batches
  consume a sequence number; heartbeat (`META::PING`/`PONG`) and request
  batches (`META::RESYNC`, `META::ENVIRONMENT`, events) carry `0` and never
  advance it.
- **Consumer**: the first guest → host batch establishes a baseline
  (`expected = sequence + 1`). Every later guest → host batch MUST satisfy
  `sequence == expected`; then `expected = sequence + 1`. A batch whose
  sequence does not match means one or more batches were lost.
- **Recovery**: on a gap the consumer MUST NOT apply the gapped batch (its
  deltas assume the lost state) and MUST request a full snapshot
  (`META::RESYNC`), then re-baseline on the next guest → host batch. The
  consumer also re-baselines on every (re)connect.
- **Heartbeat batches are exempt**: a `META::PONG` (host → guest) is not part of
  the guest → host stream; consumers track only guest → host batches.

The recovery is **always a full snapshot**, never retransmission: the renderer
is stateless and the application owns the retained tree, so a `META::RESYNC`
reconverges the consumer regardless of what was lost. **Acknowledgements and a
retransmit queue are deliberately not part of the protocol** — they would add a
per-session send buffer and an ack exchange to a design whose recovery is
already a stateless snapshot.

### Transport heartbeat

The **network batch backend** (a WebSocket / streamed connection) can fail
silently: a proxy or load balancer may drop the connection without a close
frame, or the peer's send path may wedge, leaving the socket "open" while
nothing is delivered. Neither side can detect this from the batch stream alone.
The heartbeat is the transport-liveness mechanism for this backend:

- **Probe**: the guest (client) sends a `META::PING` batch at a fixed cadence
  (default **every 5 s**). `A/B/C = 0`, no string section.
- **Reply**: the host (server) MUST answer each `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  batch as promptly as its send path allows.
- **Liveness**: a peer's *liveness* is any received batch — deltas, `PONG`, or
  anything else. A guest that receives no batch for **more than two probe
  intervals** SHOULD treat the connection as dead: close it and reconnect (the
  reconnect flow already re-syncs via `META::RESYNC`).
- **Host-side detection**: a host MAY additionally send WebSocket-protocol-level
  ping frames (browsers auto-answer) to detect a dead client and keep
  middleboxes from timing the connection out; a host whose send fails (or a
  probe that is never answered) SHOULD close the connection so the client
  reconnects instead of stalling.
- **Scope**: the heartbeat is **transport liveness only, NOT app state**. A
  `META::PING`/`META::PONG` batch MUST NOT be routed into the application — it
  never touches the retained tree, signals, or events. The **shared-memory ring
  backend MUST NOT use it**: ring peers are co-located and their liveness is the
  host process's concern, so the ring never carries, expects, or relays
  `META::PING`/`META::PONG`.

That’s the WebSocket transport heartbeat, not app activity.

- `META 0x4` = category `META` (`0x04`), command `PING` (`0x04`)
- `META 0x5` = category `META` (`0x04`), command `PONG` (`0x05`)
- `a=0,b=0,c=0` = empty payload
- `seq=0` = heartbeats are exempt from the delta sequence counter

Yes — indirectly. The `PING`/`PONG` payload itself is empty and carries no styles. The problem is that the DOM client currently runs **every inbound batch through `applyBatch`**, including `PONG`.

- `lib/typescript/src/transport.ts:258` calls `applyBatch(batch, renderer)` for all batches.
- `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:460` always ends with `applyLayout(renderer)`.
- `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:192` then re-applies derived inline layout styles such as `width`/`height` fills, `z-index`, `grid-row`/`grid-column`, `grid-template-columns`, `justify-self`, and `align-self`.

So if your DevTools edit touches one of those renderer-owned properties, it is overwritten about every 5 seconds. Edits to unrelated properties such as `color`, `background`, `padding`, or `font-size` should persist.

This also conflicts with the heartbeat contract in `spec/OPCODE.md`: `PING`/`PONG` is transport-liveness only and **must not be routed into the application/renderer**.

Suggested fix:
1. Treat a single-opcode `META::PONG` batch as transport-only in `transport.ts` and skip `applyBatch` (and probably `onBatch`).
2. Defensively make `applyBatch` skip `applyLayout` when a batch contains no layout-affecting `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes.
3. Add a transport test proving a `PONG` batch does not touch DOM styles.

It doesn’t keep a copy of your DevTools styles. It keeps references to the same live DOM elements and recomputes a few derived properties from their current state.

What is retained:

- `renderer.byId` — `nodeId → DOM element`, built at boot from `[data-pathland-id]` (`lib/typescript/src/index.ts:74`) and updated by tree deltas.
- `componentByNode` — `element → component type` WeakMap (`apply.ts:130`), set when `CREATE_NODE` is applied (`apply.ts:661`). Used to decide whether an element is a stack, ZStack, grid, etc.
- The DOM itself holds the app-emitted inline styles. There is no separate renderer-side style map; `applyStyle` writes directly to `el.style`.
- The server’s canonical retained tree exists, but `PONG` does not carry it. Only a `RESYNC` would resend the tree.

Why a heartbeat can reset edits:

1. `PONG` arrives.
2. `transport.ts` does not treat it as transport-only: it calls `applyBatch(...)` (`transport.ts:258`).
3. `applyBatch` processes the no-op META opcode, then always calls `applyLayout(renderer)` (`apply.ts:460`).
4. `applyLayout` recomputes from the DOM/component map and unconditionally writes some properties:
   - `align-self` for FILL children (`apply.ts:329`)
   - ZStack child `justify-self`, `align-self`, `z-index` (`apply.ts:224-235`)
   - grid `grid-row`, `grid-column`, `justify-self`, `align-self`, `z-index` (`apply.ts:256-265`)

So those specific renderer-owned properties get overwritten every heartbeat. Edits to unrelated CSS (`color`, `padding`, `font-size`, etc.) should survive. If **every** change resets, look for a page reload/HMR instead — the heartbeat path only rewrites derived layout properties.

Because `align-self:stretch` is not chosen by “this is an HStack.” It is applied only when that HStack is considered **FILL** on its parent’s cross axis.

The rule is in `fillsAxis` (`lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:151`):

- A component is FILL if it has `width/height: 100%`, is a greedy primitive, or is a stack whose subtree contains a greedy/FILL descendant.
- `Spacer` is greedy on its parent’s **main axis** (`apply.ts:166-170`).
- `ScrollView` is treated as greedy on **both** axes.
- `maxWidth` does **not** count as FILL; it is only a cap.

For the two HStacks in `DocsSite.kt`:

- **Line 87 HStack**: children are a `VStack` capped with `maxWidth(620f)` and an `Image` capped with `maxWidth(520f)`. Neither is greedy. `fillsAxis` returns false → no `width:100%`, no `align-self:stretch`.
- **Line 148 HStack**: contains `Spacer()` at lines 149 and 164. `Spacer` is greedy on the HStack’s horizontal main axis, so the HStack itself becomes FILL horizontally. The parent `VStack` then sees a cross-axis fill child and sets `align-self:stretch` (`apply.ts:321-330`). It also gets `width:100%` from `apply.ts:202-209`.

The `height:100%` on the second one comes from `CodeBlock` → `ScrollView`; `COMPONENT_SCROLLVIEW` is treated as greedy on both axes, so vertical fill propagates up through the `VStack` into that HStack.

If you want the first HStack to stretch too, give it an explicit FILL width, e.g. `frame(width = Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` (the DSL maps infinity to `FILL`), rather than only `maxWidth`.

a stack reads a single axis (a `VStack` the horizontal component, an `HStack`
  the vertical — codes `0/1/2`), a `ZStack`/grid both axes. With no `ALIGNMENT`
  (code `0`/absent) the default cross-axis position is the **start**. Code `3`
  is `top-center`, never a stretch; stretching lives in the **child's size
  kind** (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = `FILL`).
- Only a **`Fill`-sized child** fills the container's cross size.
- **The default is *hug*, not stretch.** A child with no cross-axis size is NOT
  stretched to fill the cross axis. This deliberately matches **SwiftUI**
  (children report their ideal size; a `VStack`/`HStack` aligns them) and
  **Compose** (Row/Column children wrap content cross-axis unless
  `fillMaxWidth/Height`), rather than CSS flexbox's `align-items: stretch`
  default. A renderer must therefore NOT stretch cross-axis children implicitly
  (e.g. the web renderer uses `align-items: flex-start`, not the flex default).

### Layout-greedy primitives

The cross-axis hug default has **four intrinsic exceptions** — primitives whose
native behavior is to fill space (SwiftUI/Compose precedent), so an app does not
need an explicit `FILL` frame to get their natural behavior:

| Primitive | Greedy on | Precedent |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| `DIVIDER` | cross-axis | SwiftUI `Divider()` fills the stack's available width/height; CSS `hr` is block-width |
| `SCROLLVIEW` | its **scroll axis** only (`SCROLL_AXIS`, default vertical) | SwiftUI `ScrollView` expands along its scroll axis; the cross axis hugs its content unless a `Fill` child propagates |
| `COLOR` | both axes | SwiftUI `Color` is layout-greedy and expands unless a frame constrains it |
| `SPACER` | main-axis | `Spacer()` absorbs leftover main-axis space by definition |

Rules:

- Greedy fills **only the axis the primitive is designed to fill** — never both
  for `DIVIDER`/`SPACER`/`SCROLLVIEW`; a `SCROLLVIEW` fills its scroll axis and
  **hugs on the cross axis** (a `Fill`-width content child propagates `Fill`).
- An **explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` always overrides** the greedy default (`Fixed`
  = that box; `FILL` = stretch anyway; `HUG_CONTENT` = natural size).
- Every other primitive (Text, Image, stacks, buttons, controls) is a plain
  **Fixed / Fill / Hug** node governed by the size model — no implicit
  greediness.

### Non-visual nodes (layout-transparent)
|---|-------|-------------------|----------|
| C1 | `Image` `WIDTH=44, HEIGHT=44` | a row with leftover space | exactly `44×44` points (not the content's intrinsic size, not stretched) |
| C2 | Fixed `220×220` child | a `280`-wide column, cross axis | exactly `220` on the cross axis, aligned (not filled to `280`) |
| C3 | `Fill`-height container | a `HUG`-height child | the child keeps its natural height; leftover stays empty / goes to a `Fill` sibling |
| C4 | Composite button, no frame | a `Fill`-height column | content height (not absorbed/stretched to the viewport) |
| C5 | Hug `Text` | a stack | natural size on both axes (not stretched cross-axis) |
| C6 | Fixed-width `VStack` | fixed `200` box, taller children | children lay out within `200`; overflow is visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it |
| C7 | `Text` `WIDTH=120`, longer content | a column | wraps at word boundaries within `120`; natural height = line count × line height |
| C8 | `Text` long content, `LINE_LIMIT=2` | a `200`-wide column | at most 2 lines; overflow on the last visible line tail-ellipsized (`…`) |
| C9 | `Text` `LINE_LIMIT=1`, `TRUNCATION_MODE=Head` | a `200`-wide column | single line, ellipsis at the start, the tail preserved |
| C10 | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=1` | a Fixed box with overflowing content | content (and the node's painted decoration) clipped to the allocated box; layout unchanged |
| C11 | `Grid` `GRID_COLUMNS=2`, `SPACING=8`, Hug cells | a definite-width parent | two **equal `1fr` columns** with an 8pt gap; Hug cells keep their natural size, positioned at Leading in their track |

The code block is still forcing the section to fill.

`LandingPlayground` contains `CodeBlock`, which contains a horizontal `ScrollView`. In the current renderer `fills_axis` treats `SCROLLVIEW` as greedy on **both** axes (`lib/typescript/src/apply.ts:166-170` and `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/src/lib.rs:697`), and that fill propagates:

```
ScrollView → CodeBlock VStack → LandingPlayground HStack
           → content VStack → outer HStack
```

Removing the `Spacer`s removed one fill source, but not the ScrollView one. The SSR confirms it:

```html
<div data-pathland-id="40" style="...;width:100%;height:100%;align-self:stretch;">
  <div data-pathland-id="41" style="...;width:100%;height:100%;align-self:stretch;">
```

`#41` is full-width because the code block fills. It has `align-items:flex-start`, so its text starts at the left. The parent VStack’s `align-items:center` can’t center a child that is already `width:100%`.

## Quick fix

Give the content block a finite width so it stops being treated as FILL. In `DocsSite.kt` around line 162:

```kotlin
VStack {
    ...
}
.frame(width = 620f)   // was: .frame { maxWidth(620f) }
```

Then `fills_axis` returns false for that child, the outer HStack hugs its content, and the parent `VStack(alignment = CENTER)` centers it. The HStack will be roughly `620 + 80` padding wide.

Caveat: fixed width is not responsive, and the section may still get `height:100%` until the ScrollView cross-axis greed is fixed.

## Proper fix

Implement the layout spec faithfully:

1. Make `SCROLLVIEW` greedy only on `SCROLL_AXIS` — horizontal scroll fills width, but its height hugs (`spec/LAYOUT.md` C13/C14). This removes the incorrect `height:100%`.
2. Treat `maxWidth`/`maxHeight` as a bounded flexible frame: cap the size but keep the box aligned by the parent’s `ALIGNMENT` instead of forcing `align-self:stretch`.
3. Apply the same logic in the Rust HTML renderer, TypeScript DOM renderer, and Java HTML port, with conformance tests.

Then `.frame { maxWidth(620f) }` will work as expected and the section will center responsively.

Which approach do you want: the immediate fixed-width change, or the renderer/layout fix?
Do renderer/layout fix. Ensure the spec is cirrect first.
