# Pathland Layout Allocation Contract

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 1, 2026

---

## Purpose

This document pins down the **allocation semantics** of the size/frame
properties (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, `ALIGNMENT`, `CONTENT_MODE`, and the `FILL` /
`HUG_CONTENT` sentinels) so that **the same frame produces the same logical-points
layout on every renderer** (HTML, GTK4, and any future SwiftUI/Compose target).
The protocol's sizes are **logical points** (SwiftUI points / Compose `dp` / CSS
pixels) — see the units note in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) — and this contract
defines what a frame *means*, not how many device pixels it is.

The wire format is unchanged by this document. It is a **contract clarification**:
renderers are aligned to it incrementally (their implementation status lives in
each project's `status.md`, not here).

- Wire format and value types: [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
- View catalog: [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)
- Modifiers (the `frame` DSL surface): [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md)

> **Implementation status** is tracked per implementing project (a `status.md`
> in each protocol crate/library), **not** in this specification. This document
> defines the protocol contract only.

---

## The size model

Each axis (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`) of every view carries exactly one of three size
kinds:

| Kind | Wire value | Meaning | SwiftUI | Compose | CSS |
|------|-----------|---------|---------|---------|-----|
| **Fixed** | a finite positive `F32` | The view occupies **exactly that many points** on the axis. Content fits *inside* the box; a smaller parent constrains it (a `ScrollView` enables overflow). | `.frame(width: 44, height: 44)` | `Modifier.size(44.dp)` / `.width(…)` / `.height(…)` | `width: 44px; height: 44px` |
| **Fill** | `-1` (`FILL`, also `∞` normalized to it) | The view **expands to fill the available space** on the axis — it absorbs the parent's leftover space. | `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` | `Modifier.fillMaxWidth()` / `fillMaxHeight()` | flex `flex-grow` / `100%` |
| **Hug** | `-2` (`HUG_CONTENT`) or **absent** | The view takes its **natural / intrinsic** size on the axis. | ideal size (`.fixedSize()` forces it) | `Modifier.wrapContentWidth()` / `height(IntrinsicSize.Min)` | `fit-content` / auto |

Notes:

- **`HUG_CONTENT` and absent are the same size kind.** A view with no `WIDTH`/
  `HEIGHT` property behaves as `HUG_CONTENT` on that axis.
- **Fixed is a hard allocation, not a minimum or a hint.** A renderer must not
  over-allocate a Fixed view beyond its box because the parent has extra space,
  and must not under-allocate it below its box when the parent can provide it
  (a smaller parent constrains it — a parent always has the final say, as in all
  three reference frameworks).
- **Content is fitted within the box** (see [Content fitting](#content-fitting)),
  never used to grow the box.

---

## Container allocation rules

Containers (`VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/`ZSTACK`, `GRID`, `SCROLLVIEW`, and the semantic
composites) allocate their children by these rules. The **main axis** is the
container's layout direction; the **cross axis** is the other one.

### Main axis

A child's main-axis size comes from its size kind:

- **Fixed** → the child is allocated exactly its box.
- **Fill** → the child expands; **leftover main-axis space goes only to `Fill`
  children** (shared between them). A container with no `Fill` child leaves the
  leftover space empty at the end of its main axis.
- **Hug** (or absent) → the child's natural size, positioned at the start of
  the leftover space.

### Cross axis

- A **Fixed** or **Hug** child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
  **positioned** by the container's `ALIGNMENT`.
- **`ALIGNMENT` positions but never resizes.** It selects the placement of
  Fixed/Hug children within leftover space; it does not stretch them. The value
  is a **2D position code** (the [ZStack table](./PRIMITIVES.md#zstack--zstack-0x12)):
  a stack reads a single axis (a `VStack` the horizontal component, an `HStack`
  the vertical — codes `0/1/2`), a `ZStack`/grid both axes. With no `ALIGNMENT`
  (code `0`/absent) the default cross-axis position is the **start**. Code `3`
  is `top-center`, never a stretch; stretching lives in the **child's size
  kind** (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = `FILL`).
- Only a **`Fill`-sized child** fills the container's cross size.
- **The default is *hug*, not stretch.** A child with no cross-axis size is NOT
  stretched to fill the cross axis. This deliberately matches **SwiftUI**
  (children report their ideal size; a `VStack`/`HStack` aligns them) and
  **Compose** (Row/Column children wrap content cross-axis unless
  `fillMaxWidth/Height`), rather than CSS flexbox's `align-items: stretch`
  default. A renderer must therefore NOT stretch cross-axis children implicitly
  (e.g. the web renderer uses `align-items: flex-start`, not the flex default).

### Layout-greedy primitives

The cross-axis hug default has **four intrinsic exceptions** — primitives whose
native behavior is to fill space (SwiftUI/Compose precedent), so an app does not
need an explicit `FILL` frame to get their natural behavior:

| Primitive | Greedy on | Precedent |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|
| `DIVIDER` | cross-axis | SwiftUI `Divider()` fills the stack's available width/height; CSS `hr` is block-width |
| `SCROLLVIEW` | its **scroll axis** only (`SCROLL_AXIS`, default vertical) | SwiftUI `ScrollView` expands along its scroll axis; the cross axis hugs its content unless a `Fill` child propagates |
| `COLOR` | both axes | SwiftUI `Color` is layout-greedy and expands unless a frame constrains it |
| `SPACER` | main-axis | `Spacer()` absorbs leftover main-axis space by definition |

Rules:

- Greedy fills **only the axis the primitive is designed to fill** — never both
  for `DIVIDER`/`SPACER`/`SCROLLVIEW`; a `SCROLLVIEW` fills its scroll axis and
  **hugs on the cross axis** (a `Fill`-width content child propagates `Fill`).
- An **explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` always overrides** the greedy default (`Fixed`
  = that box; `FILL` = stretch anyway; `HUG_CONTENT` = natural size).
- Every other primitive (Text, Image, stacks, buttons, controls) is a plain
  **Fixed / Fill / Hug** node governed by the size model — no implicit
  greediness.

### Non-visual nodes (layout-transparent)

Some nodes exist in the retained tree but render **no** element and take part in
**no** layout. They are **layout-transparent**:

- They are **not slots**: a stack/grid parent MUST NOT allocate space to them and
  MUST NOT contribute spacing for them (they are skipped entirely, as if absent).
- They have no box, no intrinsic size, and no content mode; `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` and
  alignment do not apply.
- Their position in the tree carries **no layout meaning** — applications place
  them for lifetime stability, not for geometry.

| Node | Role |
|------|------|
| `COMMENT` 0x7F | Opaque/debug marker |
| `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 | Owns a media resource + transport; referenced by a `VIDEO` surface ([MEDIA.md](./MEDIA.md)) |

Audio has no node at all: an audio playback is a controller plus the
application's own views, which are ordinary layout nodes.

### A container that is itself Fixed

A container with a **Fixed** `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` is allocated exactly that box and
lays its children out *within* it. A Fixed box **constrains layout but does not
clip**: content that overflows it is drawn outside the box unless
`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it (SwiftUI `.clipped()` parity); it scrolls instead
when the container is a `SCROLLVIEW`.

### Rationale

These rules are the bugs-fixed-and-avoided model of the reference renderers:

- A **Fixed image** in a row stays its box (never scaled to content or stretched
  by a tall row).
- A **Fixed/Hug child in a `Fill` container** keeps its size; leftover space
  goes to `Fill` children (or stays empty).
- A **composite button** (e.g. a library row) sizes to its content on the main
  axis unless the node is explicitly `Fill`.

---

## Content fitting, truncation & clipping

Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:

- **Media** (`IMAGE`, `VIDEO`): fitted per `CONTENT_MODE` — `Fit` (0) scales to
  contain (letterboxed), `Fill` (1) scales to cover (cropped). The box is the
  allocation, never the content's intrinsic size. A `VIDEO` surface's playback
  lives on a separate `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` node; audio has no visual at all (§
  Non-visual nodes) and is controlled by the application's own views.

### Text

- **Wrapping.** An unconstrained `TEXT` lays out on a **single line at its
  natural width**. It **wraps at word boundaries only when its width is
  constrained** — a Fixed `WIDTH`, or a `LINE_LIMIT` that needs multiple lines.
  An unbreakable word wider than the box may break by character. A wrapped
  Text's natural height is its **line count × line height** (so a Hug container
  can compute its size). A Fixed `HEIGHT` constrains the box; overflow follows
  the overflow rules ([above](#a-container-that-is-itself-fixed)).
- **`LINE_LIMIT`.** A positive `LINE_LIMIT` (N) clamps the rendered text to **at
  most N lines**; any overflow beyond the last visible line is replaced by an
  ellipsis `…` at its end (**tail** truncation). `0`/absent = unlimited. It does
  not force a single line — lines are formed by wrapping at the available width
  and by explicit line breaks.
- **`TRUNCATION_MODE`.** `Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2 **positions the
  ellipsis** (at the start / middle / end of the last visible line) whenever a
  `LINE_LIMIT` clamp truncates. It applies **only when such a clamp truncates**:
  on its own it has **no observable effect** (SwiftUI-aligned) — it never forces
  a single line and never truncates by itself.

### Clipping — `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`

`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` (0x1010, U8) is a **post-layout visual clip**: the node's
content and its own painted decoration (fills, backgrounds, borders) are
clipped to its **allocated bounds box** — on **both axes**. Layout is
unaffected: the node is still allocated and positioned exactly as if unclipped;
only what is painted is clipped. `0`/absent = no clipping. A `SHAPE_KIND`
(0x0006) carried alongside constrains the clip to that geometry instead of the
plain bounds box (a bare `.clipped()` is `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` with no shape, so the
clip is the bounds box). A `SCROLLVIEW` scrolls its content rather than
clipping it.

### Containers

Stacks, scroll, and other containers lay their children out inside; a Fixed box
constrains them (scroll for `SCROLLVIEW`, otherwise overflow is visible unless
`CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it).

### Size that fits (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17)

A fit slot is **size-taking on both axes**: it stretches to its parent's
proposal (`FILL` semantics — never hugs), because its **allocated width is the
unit of fitting**. It holds at most one (selected) child in the live form, laid
out normally inside the box; a **full-snapshot emission** (the web SSR first
document) carries every candidate and the renderer lays each one out, selecting
the visible branch by CSS container queries keyed to the slot's own width (a
no-JS correct first paint — see [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md#size-that-fits)).
The renderer measures its allocated width and derives the fit index (threshold
rule in [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md#size-that-fits)). No content-based
measurement of candidates is ever done or transmitted — the query thresholds are
app-declared, so the pick is a pure function of `(thresholds, allocated width)`.

---

## Conformance cases

These are golden vectors derived from real cross-renderer divergences. For each
case, **the same frame must yield the same logical-points size on every
renderer** (HTML + GTK4 today; SwiftUI/Compose as they land).

| # | Frame | Container context | Expected |
|---|-------|-------------------|----------|
| C1 | `Image` `WIDTH=44, HEIGHT=44` | a row with leftover space | exactly `44×44` points (not the content's intrinsic size, not stretched) |
| C2 | Fixed `220×220` child | a `280`-wide column, cross axis | exactly `220` on the cross axis, aligned (not filled to `280`) |
| C3 | `Fill`-height container | a `HUG`-height child | the child keeps its natural height; leftover stays empty / goes to a `Fill` sibling |
| C4 | Composite button, no frame | a `Fill`-height column | content height (not absorbed/stretched to the viewport) |
| C5 | Hug `Text` | a stack | natural size on both axes (not stretched cross-axis) |
| C6 | Fixed-width `VStack` | fixed `200` box, taller children | children lay out within `200`; overflow is visible unless `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` clips it |
| C7 | `Text` `WIDTH=120`, longer content | a column | wraps at word boundaries within `120`; natural height = line count × line height |
| C8 | `Text` long content, `LINE_LIMIT=2` | a `200`-wide column | at most 2 lines; overflow on the last visible line tail-ellipsized (`…`) |
| C9 | `Text` `LINE_LIMIT=1`, `TRUNCATION_MODE=Head` | a `200`-wide column | single line, ellipsis at the start, the tail preserved |
| C10 | `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS=1` | a Fixed box with overflowing content | content (and the node's painted decoration) clipped to the allocated box; layout unchanged |
| C11 | `Grid` `GRID_COLUMNS=2`, `SPACING=8`, Hug cells | a definite-width parent | two **equal `1fr` columns** with an 8pt gap; Hug cells keep their natural size, positioned at Leading in their track |
| C12 | `Grid` `GRID_COLUMNS=2` with a `FILL`-width cell | a definite-width parent | the `FILL` cell **stretches to fill its column**; Hug cells keep their size; the grid does **not** propagate the `FILL` up to a Hug parent on the auto axis |
| C13 | `ScrollView` (`SCROLL_AXIS=Vertical`, no frame) | a `FILL`-sized column, content `FILL`-width | fills the available height (scroll axis); the cross (horizontal) axis hugs — it fills only because the content has a `Fill`-width child; content taller than the viewport **scrolls**, never clips or overflows the viewport |
| C14 | `ScrollView` `HEIGHT=HUG_CONTENT` | a Hug column | the viewport's height is the content's **natural height** (no vertical scroll); the cross axis hugs its content (no implicit width greed) |

Grid/scroll/lazy allocation is specified in [PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView](./PRIMITIVES.md#grid--grid-0x13); the lazy containers are identical to their eager base with windowed realization only.

Conformance tests (golden vectors) are wired in the renderer alignment passes
that follow this document; see each project's `status.md`.

| `ENUM` | 0x06 | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | 0x07 | packed `0xAARRGGBB` (sRGB) |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | 0x08 | arenaRef (token path) |

Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1.0` = `FILL` (expand to available), `-2.0` =
`HUG_CONTENT` (native intrinsic size).

> **`maxWidth`/`maxHeight: .infinity`**: SwiftUI's flexible frame is expressed as
> the `FILL` sentinel on `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`. DSLs accept `∞` (e.g. Rust
> `f32::INFINITY`, Java `Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY`) and normalize it to `FILL`
> before emission, so `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` ⇔ `WIDTH = FILL`. The
> renderer then expands the element to the available space.

> **Token references**: every property typed `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM`
> in the tables below MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`),
> with `C` = arenaRef to a token path — so modifiers like `.foregroundStyle`,

> accept either a literal or a token reference. The renderer resolves the
> reference against the [token catalog and color schemes](./TOKENS.md).

75-
76-### 1. Core Structural Classification
77-
78-Each node belongs to exactly one of the three categories above. The category
79-determines renderer responsibilities:
80-
81-- **Primitive Drawing Nodes** hold no interaction state. The server sends the
82-  full visual description; the renderer measures and paints. If a primitive has
83-  no native equivalent (e.g. `Path`), the renderer may paint it directly — this
84-  is the one case where canvas-style painting is permitted.
85-- **Semantic Control Nodes** carry intent + two-way bindings (`BINDING_ID`),
86-  accessibility traits, and local interaction physics. Their *visual chrome* is
87-  delegated per the Dual-Mode rules below; their *interaction semantics* are
88-  always renderer-owned and reported as raw events.

90-### 2. Dual-Mode Rendering Pipeline & Platform Delegation
91-
92-Every semantic control node renders in **one of two modes**, decided by whether
93-the node has a child layout tree:
94-
95-#### Native Token Mode (Leaf Control)
96-
97-When a semantic control node has **no child layout tree** (`childrenIds` is
98-empty), the client platform **MUST delegate rendering entirely to its native OS
99-control** — `Button`, `TextField`/`SecureField`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
100-`DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`, `Picker`, and `Menu` each map to the platform's
101-native control (the concrete widget per renderer lives in that renderer's
102-`status.md`).
103-
104-**System style modifiers act as visual style tokens** — they force the platform
105-to switch native control variants **without emitting child nodes over the
106-wire**. Example: `TOGGLE_STYLE = CHECKBOX` renders `Toggle` (0x24) as a native
107-checkbox; `TOGGLE_STYLE = SWITCH` (default) as a native switch; `TOGGLE_STYLE =
108-BUTTON` as a toggle button.
109-
110-#### Composite Override Mode (Container Control)
111-
112-When a semantic control **contains child nodes** (or a custom style body is
113-defined on the server), the client platform **MUST**:
114-
115-1. **Suppress** its default native control visuals (the OS control chrome).

### ScrollView — `SCROLLVIEW` 0x14

A scrollable content container. **Layout-greedy on its scroll axis** — it fills
the available space on that axis so the content can scroll; on the **cross axis**
it **hugs its content** by default (it shrinks to fit the content, SwiftUI
`ScrollView` semantics). An explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides either behavior
(LAYOUT.md §layout-greedy primitives).

**Properties**: `SCROLL_AXIS` (0x0021, F32 enum: `Vertical`=0 — the default when
absent, `Horizontal`=1) selects the scroll axis; plus layout modifiers
(Fixed/Fill frames, `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS` as an inset).

**Content.** The **first child** is the content; a scroll view carries a single
content subtree (typically a stack), matching SwiftUI/Compose's single-content
contract. The content is measured with an **unbounded proposal on the scroll
axis** — it may grow beyond the viewport (that is what scrolls) — and a
**bounded proposal on the cross axis** (the viewport's cross size). **Fill
propagation applies on the cross axis**: a `Fill`-width child of the content
stack (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` in SwiftUI) is itself `Fill`-sized and
fills the viewport on that axis — so a full-width scroll row is authored as a
`Fill`-width child, never by stretching the content or the viewport. Content
with no `Fill` child keeps its natural cross size, and the viewport hugs/shrinks
to fit it. The **viewport** is the scroll view's allocated box; a Hug
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` — or a Hug parent proposal on an axis — sizes the viewport to
the content's natural size on that axis (the viewport fits the content, so that
axis does not scroll).

**Overflow.** A scroll view scrolls its content rather than clipping it — the
viewport clips by virtue of scrolling; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` on the scroll view has
no further effect on the content.

**Events.** With the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8) the renderer reports the
content offset in logical points via `EVENT::SCROLL`; with `WHEEL` (bit 9) it
reports wheel/trackpad deltas via `EVENT::WHEEL` (both draft — see
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)).

off-screen cells until scrolled into view and MAY discard realized cells that
leave the viewport. Realization never changes layout — a cell's position is
always its row-major index in the full cell list. Typically nested inside a
`SCROLLVIEW`.

# Plan: spec-first ScrollView / frame-bounds layout fix

## Spec audit — what is already correct

`spec/LAYOUT.md` already states the right contract:

- `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy **only on its scroll axis**; the cross axis hugs and only fills via a `Fill` content child (`LAYOUT.md:105`, C13/C14).
- `ALIGNMENT` positions, never stretches; only FILL children stretch.
- `PRIMITIVES.md §ScrollView` matches that.

The renderers are the inconsistent part:

- Rust HTML: `fills_axis` treats `SCROLLVIEW` as greedy on both axes (`lib/rust/.../lib.rs:697`), emits unconditional `flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch` (`:2095`), and ignores `SCROLL_AXIS`.
- Java HTML port: same (`HtmlRenderer.java:743`, `RenderNode.java:519`).
- TS DOM: same (`apply.ts:166-170`, `elements.ts:91-98`).
- GTK: documents `SCROLL_AXIS` as a gap (`render-gtk/status.md`).
- Qt: already implements axis-aware ScrollView greed (`qt_layer.cpp:1044`), so it is the reference for that part.

## Spec corrections needed first

### 1. Add a “Frame bounds” section to `spec/LAYOUT.md`

Bounds (`MIN_*`, `IDEAL_*`, `MAX_*`) currently have no layout contract at all; the docs only say they are emitted. Define:

- Bounds are constraints layered on top of the size kind, not new size kinds.
- Resolution order per axis: base size kind/intrinsic size → apply bounds → position.
- `MIN_*` raises the resolved size; `MAX_*` caps it; if `MIN > MAX`, `MIN` wins.
- A finite `MAX_*` makes the axis **bounded**:
  - A `Fill` or greedy node still fills/grows up to the cap.
  - A `Hug` node remains Hug, capped by the max.
  - A bounded node does **not** propagate an unbounded fill to ancestors.
  - A bounded node is **not** given cross-axis stretch; once capped, it is positioned by the parent’s `ALIGNMENT`.
- `IDEAL_*`: recommended spec choice is an advisory Hug preference; v1 renderers may ignore it rather than treating it as Fixed. This fixes the current CSS mapping where `IDEAL_WIDTH` overwrites `WIDTH`.
- `MAX_* = ∞` means “no constraint” and is omitted; `WIDTH/HEIGHT = ∞` means `FILL`.

### 2. Resolve the infinity contradiction

`MODIFIERS.md:67` says `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` ⇔ `WIDTH=FILL`; `DSL.md:850` says infinite `maxWidth` in the bounds builder means “no limit.” Clarify:

- Canonical SwiftUI `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` is represented as `WIDTH=FILL`.
- The explicit `MAX_WIDTH`/`MAX_HEIGHT` properties are finite bounds only; an infinite value is omitted.
- Update the DSL sentence to match.

### 3. Tighten ScrollView wording

Add to `PRIMITIVES.md §ScrollView` and `LAYOUT.md`:

- A finite `MAX_*` on the scroll axis caps the viewport’s greedy size.
- A finite `MAX_*` on the cross axis caps content fill propagation; the viewport is positioned by the parent’s `ALIGNMENT`.

`Align` positions a child within itself according to `Alignment` (e.g., `Alignment.topRight` ), and by default sizes itself to fill available space. `Center` is just `Align` with `Alignment.center` .

Forces exact width/height (tight constraints), or use `SizedBox.expand()` / `SizedBox.shrink()` . Also commonly used as a spacer:

`ConstrainedBox` adds **additional** constraints (it intersects with what the parent gives, doesn't override).

We can specify along which axes a scroll view should scroll. The default is vertical. While a vertical scroll view always becomes exactly as tall as proposed, it has infinite vertical space available for its contents. During layout, a vertical scroll passes on its own proposed width, but it proposes nil for the height to its children. In other words, it tells its children to become their ideal height.

Note that the green color has an ideal height , which gets used when the stack proposes a nil height. (If you're wondering why the VStack first propagates to the padded text, it's because it's the least flexible child.)

        "Depending on the relationship a view needs to have with its container, we can choose from three `containerRelativeFrame()` overloads. A view can fill the available width or height, occupy a chosen number of equal portions, or calculate a custom length from the container size. In each case, SwiftUI finds the nearest supported container, such as a window, navigation or tab container, or scroll view, and uses the space it provides after accounting for safe-area insets.

## \# Matching a container dimension

The most direct form of container-relative sizing makes a view match its container along one or more axes. Its first parameter accepts an `Axis.Set` , where we pass `.horizontal` to use the available width, `.vertical` to use the available height, or `[.horizontal, .vertical]` to match both dimensions.

For example, we can present a series of cards in a horizontal scroll view, with each card matching the width of its visible content area.

```
struct  DaysView:  View  {
     var  body:  some View  {
         let  pageMargin:  CGFloat  =  20 ScrollView (. horizontal ) {
             HStack (spacing: pageMargin) {
                 ForEach (dayForecasts) { forecast  in DayForecastCard (forecast: forecast)
                        . containerRelativeFrame (. horizontal )
                }
            }
        }
        . contentMargins (. horizontal , pageMargin)
    }
}
```

The `HStack` isn't a supported container for relative sizing, so SwiftUI continues up the view hierarchy and uses the surrounding `ScrollView` . Its horizontal content margins are removed from the available width, allowing every card to fill the visible content area while preserving space at both edges. Because we only pass the horizontal axis to `containerRelativeFrame()` , the card can determine its own height from its content or aspect ratio.

## \# Dividing a container into equal portions

Matching an entire container dimension works well when one view should fill the available space, but some layouts need to keep several items visible at once.

content.text:
## Comparison: finite `maxWidth` semantics

### SwiftUI

```swift
VStack(alignment: .center) {
    HStack { /* content */ }
        .frame(maxWidth: 620)
}
```

SwiftUI’s frame is a **flexible frame**, not just a CSS cap:

- Only `maxWidth` set: if the parent proposes more than the content size, the frame accepts the proposal **clamped to 620**. So it commonly becomes 620 wide, even when the content is smaller.
- Only `minWidth` set: the frame grows between the content size and the proposal.
- Both `minWidth` and `maxWidth`: SwiftUI clamps the **parent proposal** to that range, largely ignoring content size.
- `idealWidth` is used when the proposal for that dimension is unspecified; it is **not** a fixed width.

So SwiftUI `.frame(maxWidth: 620)` ≈ “fill up to 620,” not “hug content but never exceed 620.”

### Jetpack Compose

```kotlin
Column(horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally) {
    Box(
        modifier = Modifier.widthIn(max = 620.dp)
    ) { /* content */ }
}
```

Compose is constraint-based:

- `widthIn(max = 620.dp)` adds a max constraint; the child chooses its own size within it.
- The child **does not automatically fill** to 620. A small child stays small and is centered by the parent.
- `fillMaxWidth()` sets `minWidth = maxWidth = available`, so it fills.
- `fillMaxWidth(fraction)` fills a fraction of the available max width.
- `weight` distributes main-axis space in `Row`/`Column`.

This is a **cap/hug** model, not SwiftUI’s flexible fill-to-max model.

### Flutter

```dart
Column(
  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.center,
  children: [
    ConstrainedBox(
      constraints: const BoxConstraints(maxWidth: 620),
      child: content,
    ),
  ],
)
```

Flutter is also constraint-based:

- `ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: 620)` intersects its constraints with the parent’s; it does **not** force the child to 620.
- A small child stays small; `Center`/`Align` or `Column(crossAxisAlignment: center)` centers it.
- To fill up to 620, use a child that expands, e.g. `SizedBox(width: double.infinity)` or tight constraints.
- Flutter’s `Column` defaults to `CrossAxisAlignment.center`; Pathland’s default is start.

### Summary

| Behavior | SwiftUI `maxWidth: 620` | Compose `widthIn(max = 620.dp)` | Flutter `ConstrainedBox(maxWidth: 620)` | Proposed Pathland `MAX_WIDTH=620` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Small content in a wide parent | Expands to 620 | Stays content-sized | Stays content-sized | Stays content-sized (recommended) |
| Large content | Capped at 620 | Capped at 620 | Capped at 620 | Capped at 620 |
| Fill to available | `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` | `fillMaxWidth()` | `SizedBox(width: double.infinity)` | `WIDTH=FILL` |
| Center the capped box | Parent stack alignment | Parent alignment | Parent `Center`/`Align` | Parent `ALIGNMENT` |

**Recommendation:** make Pathland’s finite `MAX_*` match Compose/Flutter: a **cap/hug constraint**, not SwiftUI’s flexible fill-to-max. Pathland already has an explicit `FILL` kind, and the docs page’s first HStack depends on maxWidth acting as a cap. Matching SwiftUI would make both HStacks expand to their max widths and require a different centering strategy.

## Comparison: `idealWidth` / ideal size

| Framework | Equivalent | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftUI | `.frame(idealWidth:)` | A preferred size used when the proposal for that dimension is unspecified; not a fixed size. |
| Compose | No direct equivalent | Closest: `width(IntrinsicSize.Max/Min)` for intrinsic measurement, or `widthIn` bounds. |
| Flutter | No direct equivalent | Closest: `IntrinsicWidth` / `IntrinsicHeight`, or `ConstrainedBox(minWidth:)`. |
| Pathland | `IDEAL_WIDTH/HEIGHT` | Currently mapped to CSS `width/height`, which behaves like a fixed size and can overwrite `WIDTH`. |

**Recommendation:** define `IDEAL_*` as advisory. In v1, either ignore it or only use it when the axis has no proposal and no explicit size. Do **not** treat it as Fixed. This removes the current CSS ordering bug where `IDEAL_WIDTH` can overwrite `WIDTH`.

## Comparison: ScrollView cross axis

| Framework | Vertical ScrollView cross-axis width |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI | Hugs its content width unless a child fills the width; it accepts the proposed height on the scroll axis. |
| Compose | Keeps the incoming width constraints; content width unless a child uses `fillMaxWidth`. |
| Flutter | More parent/child dependent: `SingleChildScrollView` can shrink-wrap the cross axis, while `ListView` generally expands it. |
| Pathland spec | Cross axis hugs; scroll axis is greedy. This matches SwiftUI and Compose. |
| Current Pathland renderers | HTML/Java/TS/GTK treat ScrollView as greedy on both axes; Qt is already correct. |

So the existing `spec/LAYOUT.md` ScrollView rule is correct. The spec work is mainly adding the missing **frame bounds** contract, not rewriting ScrollView.

## Updated web-only plan

Scope confirmed: **web renderers now** (Rust HTML canonical, Java HTML port, TypeScript DOM), plus fixtures. Native GTK/Qt remain follow-ups.

### 1. Spec changes first

- `spec/LAYOUT.md`
  - Add a “Frame bounds” section:
    - bounds are constraints, not size kinds;
    - finite `MAX_*` is a **cap/hug** (Compose/Flutter-style), not SwiftUI’s fill-to-max;
    - a bounded axis does not propagate an unbounded fill to ancestors;
    - a bounded node is positioned by the parent’s `ALIGNMENT`, not stretched;
    - `MIN > MAX` → min wins;
    - `IDEAL_*` is advisory and not fixed.
  - Add conformance cases C15–C20 covering scroll-axis greed, bounded Hug/FILL, and ScrollView cross-axis bounds.
- `spec/MODIFIERS.md` / `spec/DSL.md`
  - Resolve the infinity wording:
    - `WIDTH/HEIGHT = ∞` → `FILL`;
    - `MIN/IDEAL/MAX = ∞` → omitted/no constraint;
    - canonical SwiftUI `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` maps to `WIDTH=FILL`.
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md`
  - Cross-reference the bounds rule in ScrollView.
- No wire/protocol ID changes; `spec/protocol.tsv` unchanged.

### 2. Rust HTML renderer

- Make `SCROLLVIEW` greed depend on `SCROLL_AXIS`.
- Detect finite `MAX_WIDTH/MAX_HEIGHT` and treat that axis as bounded:
  - no unbounded fill propagation;
  - no `align-self:stretch`;
  - parent alignment positions the capped box.
- Keep explicit `WIDTH/HEIGHT=FILL` CSS, with the max clamping it.
- Remove unconditional ScrollView `flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`; derive scroll fill from scroll axis + parent main axis.
- Emit `data-pathland-scroll-axis` for hydration.
- Add tests for C13–C20.

### 3. Java HTML port

Mirror the Rust behavior in `RenderNode.fillsAxis`, `fillPropagation`, and the ScrollView branch. Regenerate and pass `GoldenConformanceTest`.

### 4. TypeScript DOM renderer

- Implement `SCROLL_AXIS` handling and read `data-pathland-scroll-axis`.
- Make `fillsAxis` axis-aware for ScrollView.
- Treat finite max as bounded; clear `align-self` so the parent centers it.
- Remove unconditional scroll `flex/align-self`; derive scroll fill in `applyLayout`.
- Clear stale derived styles when a node stops being fill.
- Skip `applyBatch` for transport-only `META::PONG` batches.
- Add apply/transport tests.

### 5. Fixtures and verification

- Add `scrollaxis` and `maxbounds` scenarios to `pathland-html-golden`; regenerate fixtures.
- Run:
  - `cd lib/rust && cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden`
  - `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`
  - `cd lib/typescript && npm test`
  - `cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-docs,pathland-docs-demo -am test`
- Verify `http://localhost:8080/`: HStack `#40` no longer has `width:100%`, `height:100%`, or `align-self:stretch`; both HStacks are centered.

Update `pathland-render-html/status.md`, `lib/java/pathland-render-html/status.md`, `lib/typescript/status.md`, and `pathland-html-golden/status.md`. Leave GTK/Qt as documented follow-ups.

content.text:
Yes. Removing `IDEAL_*` for now is low-risk **if you treat the wire IDs as reserved, not as reusable**.

## Impact

| Area | Change | Hurt? |
|---|---|---|
| Wire protocol | Keep `IDEAL_WIDTH=0x0013`, `IDEAL_HEIGHT=0x0016` reserved | No. Old peers can still send them; renderers ignore them. |
| `protocol.tsv` | Keep the rows | No. The manifest still matches the Rust/Java constants. |
| Kotlin DSL | Remove `idealWidth` / `idealHeight` from `Frame.Config` | Only external Kotlin callers break; there are no usages in this repo. |
| Rust/Java/TS renderers | Stop mapping `IDEAL_*` to `width`/`height` | Improves correctness. The current mapping is wrong and can overwrite `WIDTH`. |
| Qt renderer | Stop applying `setPreferredWidth/Height` for `IDEAL_*` | Removes another wrong behavior. |
| Specs | Remove `idealWidth/idealHeight` from the public frame APIs; add a reserved-ID note | No wire or compatibility issue. |
| Tests | Manifest test still passes; add a test that reserved `IDEAL_*` is ignored | Straightforward. |

The main benefit: the bounds contract becomes only `MIN_*` and `MAX_*`, which is much easier to specify and implement. There is no need to define “ideal size” across SwiftUI/Compose/Flutter.

The main possible hurt is external Kotlin DSL code that already calls `idealWidth`/`idealHeight`. That is a source-compatibility break. Since the current behavior is wrong (it acts like a fixed width and can overwrite `WIDTH`), removing it is better than leaving a misleading API.

Do **not** remove/renumber the constants. Keep them as reserved IDs so a future implementation can restore `IDEAL_*` without a wire or manifest migration.

## Updated plan addition

Add this before the frame-bounds work:

1. Keep `IDEAL_WIDTH`/`IDEAL_HEIGHT` constants and manifest rows, commented as **reserved; no layout effect in v1**.
2. Remove `idealWidth`/`idealHeight` from the Kotlin `Frame.Config` DSL.
3. Remove `IDEAL_*` handling from:
   - Rust HTML `style_css`
   - Java HTML `RenderNode`
   - TS `classes.ts`
   - Qt property application
4. Remove `idealWidth/idealHeight` from `MODIFIERS.md`, `DSL.md`, and the frame-bounds section of `LAYOUT.md`; add a reserved-ID note.
5. Add a renderer test that emitting a reserved `IDEAL_*` property has no layout effect.
6. Update renderer/status docs.

Then the spec section only defines `MIN_*`/`MAX_*`:
- `MIN_*` raises the resolved size.
- `MAX_*` caps it and makes the axis bounded.
- `MIN > MAX` → min wins.
- No `IDEAL_*` semantics in v1.

This keeps the web fix focused and removes the ambiguous API instead of inventing a meaning nobody uses.

We are still in POC-mode, so we can freely change the protocol and code. Lets remove it. Also, lets commit what we have on this branch now and then crate a new branch from main to do this layout/renderer work

# Plan: commit docs work, branch from main, then remove IDEAL + fix layout

## 1. Commit the current docs work on `feat/docs-site`

Current state:

- Branch: `feat/docs-site`
- Last commit: `9a86b9bf feat(docs): add Kotlin Markdown documentation site`
- Uncommitted: Markdown docs, component/modifier pages, `LiveExamples.kt`, docs tests, docs index generator, status updates
- One suspicious file: `application.properties` has `+pathland.debug-html=true`

That debug flag looks like a local debugging change. I would **not** commit it unless you want HTML debug comments in the docs demo.

### Sequence

1. Decide on `application.properties`:
   - Recommended: discard `+pathland.debug-html=true`.
   - Or keep it and commit it separately as a debug-only change.
2. Run final docs verification:
   - `cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-docs -am test`
   - `mvn -q -pl pathland-docs-demo test`
3. Stage the docs work:
   - `lib/java/pathland-docs`
   - `lib/java/pathland-docs-demo` (excluding the debug flag unless intended)
   - deleted `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`
   - new `docs/components/`, `docs/modifiers/`, `LiveExamples.kt`, and `src/test/`
4. Review:
   - `git diff --cached --check`
   - `git diff --cached --stat`
5. Commit, suggested message:
   - `feat(docs): move docs to Markdown pages with live examples`

## 2. Create the layout branch from main

After the commit:

```bash
git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git switch -c feat/layout-frame-bounds
```

`main` is currently clean at `origin/main` (`559dcc59`). The docs commit remains on `feat/docs-site`.

Note: the docs page being fixed is not on `main`. The layout branch can be verified with golden fixtures/tests directly. Final browser verification of the docs page will happen after merging the layout branch into `feat/docs-site` (or both into `main`).

## 3. Remove IDEAL completely (POC allowed)

Because this is POC-mode, remove the properties rather than keeping them reserved.

### Protocol / generated surface

- Remove `IDEAL_WIDTH` and `IDEAL_HEIGHT` from:
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-protocol-manifest/src/main.rs`
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-ts-codegen/src/main.rs`
  - `lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/view/core/protocol/Properties.kt`
- Add a comment at the retired IDs:
  - `0x0013` and `0x0016` are retired and must not be reused.
- Regenerate:
  - `spec/protocol.tsv`
  - `lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`
- No wire version bump needed for this pre-release change.

### DSL

- Remove `idealWidth` / `idealHeight` from `lib/java/pathland-view-core/src/main/kotlin/dev/pathland/view/dsl/Modifiers.kt`.
- Reindex `Frame.Config.bounds` from 6 slots to 4:
  - `MIN_WIDTH`, `MAX_WIDTH`, `MIN_HEIGHT`, `MAX_HEIGHT`.
- Update `spec/MODIFIERS.md` and `spec/DSL.md` to remove ideal from the public frame API.

### Renderers

- Rust HTML: remove `IDEAL_*` from the bounds CSS mapping and debug property names.
- Java HTML: remove from `RenderNode` bounds mapping and `RenderDebug`.
- TS: remove `PROP_IDEAL_*` handlers from `classes.ts`.
- Qt: remove `IDEAL_*` enum cases and property handling.
- GTK: no current handling; verify no references.
- Add a regression test that raw `0x0013`/`0x0016` properties are ignored (no width/height effect).

### Specs

- `spec/LAYOUT.md`: frame-bounds section will define only `MIN_*` and `MAX_*`.
- Add a short note in `MODIFIERS.md`/`DSL.md`: `0x0013` and `0x0016` are retired, not part of the v1 surface.
- Update the affected `status.md` files.

## 4. Then implement the web layout fix on the new branch

With IDEAL gone, do the previously planned web-only work:

1. Spec-first `MAX_*` contract:
   - finite max = cap/hug (Compose/Flutter-style, recommended);
   - bounded axes do not propagate unbounded fill or cross-axis stretch;
   - parent `ALIGNMENT` positions the capped box.
2. Fix ScrollView `SCROLL_AXIS` greed in Rust HTML, Java HTML, and TS DOM.
3. Remove unconditional ScrollView cross-axis stretch.
4. Emit `data-pathland-scroll-axis` for DOM hydration.
5. Add `scrollaxis` / `maxbounds` golden fixtures.
6. Skip `applyBatch` for `META::PONG` so heartbeats do not re-run layout.
7. Verify:
   - `cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden`
   - `cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`
   - `cd lib/typescript && npm test`
   - `cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-docs,pathland-docs-demo -am test`

## One question

Do you want `pathland.debug-html=true` included in the docs commit, or should I discard it as a local debugging change?
Included

# Final plan

No open questions. `pathland.debug-html=true` will be included in the docs commit.

## 1. Commit docs work on `feat/docs-site`

Include all current changes:

- `lib/java/pathland-docs/**`
- `lib/java/pathland-docs-demo/**`
- `application.properties` with `pathland.debug-html=true`
- Deleted `META-INF/pathland-docs.index`
- New `docs/components/`, `docs/modifiers/`, `LiveExamples.kt`, and docs tests

Before committing:

```bash
cd lib/java
mvn -q -pl pathland-docs -am test
mvn -q -pl pathland-docs-demo test
cd ../..
git diff --check
git add lib/java/pathland-docs lib/java/pathland-docs-demo
git diff --cached --check
git diff --cached --stat
```

Commit:

```bash
git commit -m "feat(docs): add Markdown pages, live examples, and HTML debug comments"
```

This leaves `feat/docs-site` clean.

## 2. Create the layout branch from main

```bash
git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git switch -c feat/layout-frame-bounds
```

`main` is currently `559dcc59`, clean and tracking `origin/main`.

## 3. Remove IDEAL completely

POC-mode: remove the properties from the public protocol, DSL, and renderers. Retire the IDs without reuse.

### Constants / manifest / codegen

- Remove `IDEAL_WIDTH` / `IDEAL_HEIGHT` from:
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-core/src/constants.rs`
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-protocol-manifest/src/main.rs`
  - `lib/rust/crates/pathland-ts-codegen/src/main.rs`
- Add a comment at the retired slots:
  - `0x0013` and `0x0016` are retired and must not be reused.
- Regenerate:
  - `spec/protocol.tsv`
  - `lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`

### Java / Kotlin

- Remove `Properties.IDEAL_WIDTH` / `IDEAL_HEIGHT`.
- Remove `idealWidth` / `idealHeight` from `Frame.Config`.
- Resize/reindex `Frame.Config.bounds` from 6 to 4 slots:
  - `MIN_WIDTH`, `MAX_WIDTH`, `MIN_HEIGHT`, `MAX_HEIGHT`.

### Renderers

- Rust HTML: remove ideal from bounds CSS mapping and debug property names.
- Java HTML: remove from `RenderNode` bounds mapping and `RenderDebug`.
- TypeScript: remove `PROP_IDEAL_*` handlers from `classes.ts`.
- Qt: remove ideal enum cases and property handling.
- GTK: verify no references remain.
- Add regression coverage that raw `0x0013`/`0x0016` properties are ignored.

### Specs / status

- Remove ideal from `MODIFIERS.md`, `DSL.md`, and the frame-bounds section of `LAYOUT.md`.
- Add a retired-ID note.
- Update affected `status.md` files.
- Search the repo for any remaining `IDEAL_*` / `idealWidth` / `idealHeight` references.

## 4. Implement the web layout fix

Scope: Rust HTML, Java HTML, TS DOM, golden fixtures.

### Spec-first

- `MAX_*` finite = **cap/hug** (Compose/Flutter-style, not SwiftUI fill-to-max).
- A bounded axis:
  - does not propagate unbounded fill to ancestors;
  - does not get `align-self:stretch`;
  - is positioned by the parent’s `ALIGNMENT`.
- `MIN > MAX` → min wins.
- Add conformance cases C15–C20.

### Rust HTML

- Make ScrollView greed depend on `SCROLL_AXIS`.
- Detect finite `MAX_*` and treat the axis as bounded.
- Keep explicit `WIDTH/HEIGHT=FILL`; the max clamps it.
- Remove unconditional ScrollView `flex/align-self`; derive fill from scroll axis + parent main axis.
- Emit `data-pathland-scroll-axis` for DOM hydration.

### Java HTML

Mirror Rust exactly in `RenderNode.fillsAxis`, `fillPropagation`, and the ScrollView branch.

### TypeScript DOM

- Implement `SCROLL_AXIS` + hydration from `data-pathland-scroll-axis`.
- Make `fillsAxis` axis-aware.
- Treat finite max as bounded; clear `align-self` so the parent centers it.
- Remove unconditional scroll fill; derive it in `applyLayout`.
- Clear stale derived styles when a node stops being fill.
- Skip `applyBatch` for `META::PONG` heartbeats.

### Fixtures

- Add `scrollaxis` and `maxbounds` scenarios.
- Regenerate:
  ```bash
  cd lib/rust
  cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
  ```

## 5. Verification

```bash
cd lib/rust
cargo test -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden
cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit

cd ../typescript
npm test

cd ../java
mvn -q -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-docs,pathland-docs-demo -am test
```

Then integrate for browser verification:

```bash
git switch -c tmp/layout-docs-verify feat/layout-frame-bounds
git merge --no-edit feat/docs-site
cd lib/java
mvn -q -pl pathland-docs-demo -am package
java -jar pathland-docs-demo/target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar
```

Check `/`:

- HStack `#40` has no `width:100%`, `height:100%`, or `align-self:stretch`.
- Both HStacks are centered.
- No heartbeat-driven layout resets.

Delete the temporary verification branch afterward.

## Result

- `feat/docs-site`: committed docs work, including the debug-HTML flag.
- `feat/layout-frame-bounds`: spec-first IDEAL removal + web renderer/layout fix.
- `main` remains untouched until both branches are ready to merge.

### Frame bounds

`MIN_WIDTH`/`MIN_HEIGHT` and `MAX_WIDTH`/`MAX_HEIGHT` are per-axis **bounds**,
not additional size kinds. They are applied after the size kind and intrinsic
size are resolved:

1. Resolve the axis size from its kind: Fixed = its box, Fill = the available
   space, Hug = the content's natural size (plus any greedy-primitive rule

2. Apply bounds:
   - `MAX_*` caps the resolved size.
   - `MIN_*` raises the resolved size.
   - When both are present and conflict, `MIN_*` wins.
3. Position the result with the parent's `ALIGNMENT` when it is smaller than
   the available cross-axis space.

A finite `MAX_*` makes that axis **bounded**:

- A bounded `Fill` or greedy node still fills/grows, but only up to the cap.
- A bounded `Hug` node remains Hug; it does not become Fill.
- A bounded node does **not** propagate an unbounded fill demand to its
  ancestors. Ancestors size to the capped content rather than stretching to
  `100%`.
- A bounded node is **not** stretched on the cross axis. Once capped, it is
  positioned by the parent's `ALIGNMENT` (the default is start).

  for a Hug node, and `width/height: 100%` plus the max for an explicit `Fill`;
  either way, no `align-self: stretch` is added for the bounded axis.

  Inline opcode properties still override the base classes. Native `<select>`
  popups, date/color dialogs, and `<video>` controls remain UA shadow DOM, so
  their internals are best-effort; app-driven media is fully themeable.
- **Properties**: `ALIGNMENT` (cross-axis **position** — the default is hug
  (`flex-start`), never CSS `align-items:stretch`, per `spec/LAYOUT.md`; only
  `FILL`-sized children stretch via their `100%` size), `CONTENT_MARGINS`,
  `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (`FILL` → `width:100%`/`height:100%` expansion, `HUG` →
  intrinsic), the frame bounds `MIN_WIDTH`/`IDEAL_WIDTH`/`MAX_WIDTH` and the
  height equivalents (emitted on the SSR first paint, matching the DOM client),
  `PADDING` + per-edge, `COLOR`,
  `BACKGROUND_COLOR`, `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT`/`FAMILY`, `TEXT_STYLE` (the
  renderer-owned default size/weight; explicit `FONT_SIZE`/`WEIGHT` override),
  `OPACITY`, `VISIBLE`,
  `Z_INDEX`, `LINE_LIMIT` (positive → `-webkit-box`/`-webkit-line-clamp` **with
  full-area sibling when both are `z-index:auto`). Mirrored by the DOM client's
  `applyLayout`.
- **Layout contract (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: cross-axis default is **hug**
  (`flex-start`), not CSS stretch; `ALIGNMENT` positions only (`Fill`=3 → hug
  default). `DIVIDER` is greedy on the cross axis (`width:100%`); `SCROLLVIEW`
  is greedy on both axes (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch`); fixed frames emit
  exact px boxes. Conformance cases C1–C6 asserted in `lib.rs` tests.
- **Fill propagation (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §stack layout model)**: implemented —
  `fills_axis` resolves a Hug stack/ZStack containing a `FILL` child / greedy
  primitive on an axis as `FILL`, emitting `width/height:100%` on that axis, and
  cross-axis `FILL` children stretch via `align-self:stretch` (SSR + TS DOM
  client, kept canonical via the layout pass in `applyLayout`).
- **ZStack (spec/PRIMITIVES.md)**: implemented — an overlapping grid
  (`grid-area:1/1` cells); the container hugs to its largest child (`max-content`)
  unless Fixed/FILL (or fill propagation → `100%`); each child keeps its own
  size and is positioned by `ALIGNMENT` on both axes (SSR + TS DOM client).
  **Grid tracks are `minmax(0,1fr)`** (ZStack + count-generated grid tracks,
  `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with
  explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent
  `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a
  short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the
  universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy
  (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`) and renders **only its
  first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C14
  covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. the `gridrow` scenario).
- `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property).
- GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact.
- **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a
  parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables
  (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web.

# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
is GraalVM native-image compatible (no reachability/resource config for a native
library). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
  `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
  `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
  self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
  former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
- **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
  committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
  fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
  client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
- **SEO document metadata (issue #45)**: `DocumentMeta`/`render(frame, root,
  meta)` / `renderLinked(..., meta)` add canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter
  cards, and component-derived JSON-LD (WebPage + Article for `ROLE_ARTICLE`).
  Window `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION` win; the metadata values are fallbacks. The
  document output is pinned byte-for-byte against the Rust renderer's
  `document_meta.document.html` fixture.
- **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline

Already committed and clean:

- `feat/docs-site`: `36c8590e feat(docs): add Markdown pages, live examples, and HTML debug comments`
- `feat/layout-frame-bounds`: `8ede7c35 feat(layout): retire IDEAL bounds and fix scroll-axis fill`

No uncommitted changes remain.

## Objective
- Finish the web layout/renderer fix after committing the Markdown docs site: remove retired `IDEAL_*`, define/correct the frame-bounds spec, make `SCROLLVIEW` greedy only on `SCROLL_AXIS`, and fix bounded `MAX_*` fill/alignment.

## Important Details
- Repo: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland`.
- `feat/docs-site` now has commit `36c8590 feat(docs): add Markdown pages, live examples, and HTML debug comments`.
- Docs commit intentionally includes `pathland.debug-html=true` in `application.properties`.
- `main` is at `559dcc59`; new active branch is `feat/layout-frame-bounds`, created from `main`.
- POC-mode decision: remove `IDEAL_WIDTH` (`0x0013`) / `IDEAL_HEIGHT` (`0x0016`) entirely. IDs are retired and must not be reused.
- Finite `MAX_*` decision: **cap/hug** semantics, matching Compose/Flutter more than SwiftUI. A bounded axis does not propagate unbounded fill, does not get `align-self:stretch`, and is positioned by parent `ALIGNMENT`.
- `SCROLLVIEW` rule: greedy only on its `SCROLL_AXIS` (default vertical); cross axis hugs unless a `Fill` child propagates.
- `PING`/`PONG` are transport-liveness only: `PONG` must not run `applyBatch` / DOM layout.
- Web scope confirmed for this change: Rust HTML, Java HTML, TypeScript DOM, fixtures. GTK/Qt native parity remains a follow-up.
- Docs work includes live fences ` ```kotlin live=<id> `, `LiveExamples.byId`, build-time `META-INF/pathland-docs.index` via Maven Ant, and component/modifier `.md` pages.
- The reported docs layout issue: HStack `#40` should no longer render `width:100%`, `height:100%`, or `align-self:stretch`; both HStacks should center in the parent VStack.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` currently reports formatting diffs; inspect whether they are pre-existing before running a broad format.

## Work State
### Completed
- Committed all docs work on `feat/docs-site`, including debug-HTML flag.
- Created `feat/layout-frame-bounds` from `main`.
- Removed `IDEAL_*` from Rust constants, protocol manifest, TS codegen, Java `Properties`, Java `Frame.Config`, HTML renderers, TS classes, and Qt handling.
- Added retired-ID comments for `0x0013`/`0x0016`; regenerated `spec/protocol.tsv` and `lib/typescript/src/constants.ts`.
- Reindexed Kotlin `Frame.Config.bounds` from 6 to 4 slots: `MIN_WIDTH`, `MAX_WIDTH`, `MIN_HEIGHT`, `MAX_HEIGHT`.
- Updated specs: `LAYOUT.md` frame-bounds section + C15–C20, `MODIFIERS.md`, `DSL.md`, `PRIMITIVES.md`.
- Implemented Rust HTML:
  - `axis_max`, `scroll_axis_horizontal`, finite-max bounded-fill behavior.
  - axis-aware `SCROLLVIEW` greed.
  - conditional ScrollView flex, `data-pathland-scroll-axis`, no unconditional cross-axis stretch.
  - retired-IDEAL regression test.
- Mirrored Java HTML behavior in `RenderNode`/`HtmlRenderer`.
- Implemented TS DOM:
  - `PROP_SCROLL_AXIS`, SSR scroll-axis hydration attribute, axis-aware `fillsAxis`.
  - finite-max bounded fill, `align-self` clearing, ScrollView main-axis fill.
  - `SizeThatFits` alignment special-case to keep SSR conformance.
  - `PONG`-only batches skipped before `applyBatch` / `onBatch`.
- Added golden scenarios `scrollaxis` and `maxbounds`; regenerated fixtures; `layout.html` changed accordingly.
- Updated status docs for Rust HTML, Java HTML, TS, html-golden, Qt.
- Verified:
  - `cd lib/rust && cargo test -q` passed.
  - `cargo test -q -p pathland-render-html` passed with new retired-IDEAL test.
  - `cd lib/java && mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core,pathland-render-html -am test` passed.
  - `cd lib/typescript && npm test` passed.

### Active
- Layout branch is uncommitted and includes formatting cleanup.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` reported diffs; some appear in Qt/codegen files and may be pre-existing. Format only changed files or review carefully.
- Final docs-page browser verification is still pending because `feat/layout-frame-bounds` was branched from `main`, which does not contain the docs app.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Resolve formatting safely: run targeted `rustfmt` on changed Rust files or inspect `cargo fmt --all -- --check` diffs, then re-run `cargo test -q -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-html-golden`.
2. Review `git status` / `git diff --check`, stage the layout/spec/fixture changes, and commit `feat/layout-frame-bounds`.
3. Create a temporary verification branch from `feat/layout-frame-bounds`, merge `feat/docs-site`, package `pathland-docs-demo`, and verify `/` shows HStack `#40` without `width:100%` / `height:100%` / `align-self:stretch`.
4. Delete the temporary verification branch and finalize status docs.

# Pathland Media Kit

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 17, 2026

---

## Introduction

Media playback in Pathland is split into two roles:

- a **media controller** ([`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`](./PRIMITIVES.md#media-controller--media_controller-0x30)
  `0x30`) — a **non-visual** node that owns a media resource and its transport
  state (source, play/pause, position, volume, …); and
- a **video surface** ([`VIDEO`](./PRIMITIVES.md#video--video-0x0a) `0x0A`) — the
  only media *view*: it references a controller and renders its video output.

**Audio has no view of its own.** Audio is non-visual: an audio playback is a
controller plus the application's **own** views (buttons, sliders, labels) bound
to the controller's transport signals. There are **no renderer-native audio
controls** — the application defines the entire control surface in code. The
former `AUDIO` component is therefore **removed**.

Before this document, playback identity *was* the media node id: the source and
the transport properties lived on the `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node itself, and the media
events reported against it. That makes a **structural swap** of the media node —
the normal case under `SIZE_THAT_FITS`, conditional rendering, or any subtree
replacement — destroy the playback, and it makes "control the same playback from
two places" inexpressible.

The controller/surface split fixes both: playback identity is the **controller**
node id, which the emitter pins **outside** the swapping branch (typically as a
root child), so a swap re-attaches a view to a playback that never stopped — and
for audio the swapping thing is just the application's own control views.

There is **one** controller component for both audio and video — the transport is
the same thing in both cases, exactly as SwiftUI has one `AVPlayer` for both and
`VideoPlayer` is merely a view over it. **Kind is decided by the views**: a
controller with a `VIDEO` surface renders video; a controller with no media view
is audio.

This document specifies the media contract: the controller node, the video
surface binding, transport commands vs. reports, the event family, and the swap
rules. It adds **one component**, **five properties**, and **one event**, and
removes the `AUDIO` component — no new opcode category, and no change to the wire
format.

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format (16-byte opcode, categories, value types, `PLPL` batches) |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | The `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` component and the `VIDEO` surface |

---

## 1. The model

```
MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30            non-visual; owns the resource + transport
  MEDIA_SOURCE
  PLAYBACK_STATE / MEDIA_POSITION / MEDIA_VOLUME
  MEDIA_MUTED / MEDIA_LOOP / MEDIA_RATE
        ▲                                        ▲
        │ MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID                    │ bound transport signals
        │                                        │
   VIDEO 0x0A                            application views
   (renders the video output)            (buttons/sliders/labels —
                                          the ENTIRE audio control surface)
```

- The **controller** is a node in the application's retained tree, but it is
  **layout-transparent** (§2.2): it occupies no space and renders no element.
- A **video surface** is an ordinary view node wherever the application wants it
  in the layout. It names a controller with `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A). It is
  **not** a child of the controller — the relationship is a **reference**, not a
  parent/child edge. The two nodes may live anywhere in the tree, and their
  relative position carries no meaning.
- **Audio has no view.** An audio playback is controlled by ordinary application
  views whose actions/values write the controller's transport properties. Nothing
  in the protocol renders audio.
- The application **SHOULD** place a controller at a stable position that no
  structural swap removes — e.g. a sibling of (or ancestor of) the `SIZE_THAT_FITS`
  slot, or a child of the root. A controller inside a swapping branch would be
  created and destroyed with that branch, defeating the split.

### 1.1 What lives where

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| The media resource (source URL/asset) | controller — `MEDIA_SOURCE` |
| Transport state (play, seek, volume, mute, loop, rate) | controller |
| Transport **commands** from the app | controller (properties) |
| Transport **reports** to the app | controller (events target its id) |
| Whether a visual is shown, and its box/content mode | `VIDEO` surface |
| The video control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | `VIDEO` surface |
| The **audio** control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | the application's own views (no protocol surface) |
| Renderer-native vs. custom **video** controls | `VIDEO` dual mode (native when it has no children, the children when it has) |

---

## 2. The controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30

### 2.1 Protocol

- A **leaf** node: it has no children. A `VIDEO` surface references it by id;
  it is not that surface's child.
- It carries the media resource and the transport properties (§2.3).
- It is created, updated, and deleted like any other node (`TREE` `CREATE_NODE` /
  `DELETE_NODE`), so it participates in the ordinary structural diff, in a
  full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and in proxy-id remapping
  ([PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) with no media-specific machinery.
- A controller is **not** a media surface and never renders a visual.

### 2.2 Layout (MUST)

A `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` is **layout-transparent**, like `COMMENT` and the
`PROXY_VIEW` passthrough ([LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md)):

- It renders **no native element**.
- It occupies **no space**: it is excluded from its parent's allocation and
  contributes **no spacing** in a stack or grid (it is not a slot).
- It imposes no alignment, sizing, or content-mode behavior.

Its position in the tree is therefore semantically irrelevant; what matters is
**lifetime stability**, not layout. An emitter SHOULD project an application-owned
controller as a pinned root child: audio has no media view, and a `VIDEO` surface
only references the controller, so the application need not place the controller
in the tree at all. Implementations that let an application place it explicitly
MUST still keep it outside any swapping branch.

### 2.3 Transport properties

| Property | Id | Type | Meaning |
|----------|----|------|---------|
| `MEDIA_SOURCE` | `0x103B` | STRING (arena ref) | The media resource: a resource name, file path, or absolute URL. An **asset reference**, never embedded in the opcode stream. Changing it re-loads the resource (and resets position to 0 unless a `MEDIA_POSITION` is applied in the same batch). |
| `PLAYBACK_STATE` | `0x1035` | U32 (0 pause, 1 play) | Transport **command**: play/pause. |
| `MEDIA_POSITION` | `0x1036` | F32 (seconds) | Seek **command**. A change seeks; it is **not** a continuous position feed (see §4.3). |
| `MEDIA_VOLUME` | `0x1037` | F32 (0..1) | Volume **command**. |
| `MEDIA_MUTED` | `0x103C` | U8 (0/1) | Mute **command**. Independent of `MEDIA_VOLUME` (the volume value is preserved). |
| `MEDIA_LOOP` | `0x103D` | U8 (0/1) | Loop the resource on end. When set, `MEDIA_ENDED` is still reported, and playback continues from 0. |
| `MEDIA_RATE` | `0x103E` | F32 | Playback rate (1.0 = normal). 0 is equivalent to pause. |

- A controller with **no** `MEDIA_SOURCE` is valid: it is idle and reports
  nothing. The renderer MUST NOT create a playback for it.
- `PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`, `MEDIA_VOLUME`, `MEDIA_MUTED`,
  `MEDIA_LOOP`, and `MEDIA_RATE` are **commands** the application writes.
  `MEDIA_SOURCE` is the resource binding.

### 2.4 Independence from video surfaces (MUST)

A controller's playback is **independent of its video surfaces**:

- Attaching a surface does **not** start, stop, seek, or re-load playback.
- Detaching (or destroying) a surface does **not** stop playback. A controller
  with **zero** surfaces is valid and keeps playing — the application decides
  when to pause (a `PLAYBACK_STATE` write).
- One controller = **one** playback. Two surfaces referencing the same
  controller share that single playback: a transport command from either affects
  both, and the reports describe both.

---

## 3. The video surface — `VIDEO` 0x0A

`VIDEO` is the **only** media view. It names its controller with
`MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A, U32 — the controller node id) and renders that
playback's video output in its own box, fitted per `CONTENT_MODE` (`Fit`/`Fill`).
With no children it presents renderer-native video controls; with children (a
`VideoStyle`) the children are the control UI.

- **Audio has no surface.** The removed `AUDIO` component is not replaced: an
  audio playback is rendered by **nothing** in the protocol — the application's
  own views are the entire control surface (§1).
- **Multiplicity**: any number of `VIDEO` surfaces may reference one controller
  (the same playback shown in two places), and any number of controllers may
  coexist.
- **A surface carries no source.** `VIDEO_SOURCE` (0x1034) — like `AUDIO_SOURCE`
  (0x1033) — is **removed**; the source lives on the controller as `MEDIA_SOURCE`.
  A `VIDEO` with no `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` renders blank; one whose controller id
  is **unknown** (not yet created, or deleted) renders blank and MUST NOT crash —
  consistent with the unknown-component rule ([PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md)).
- A `VIDEO` whose controller has no `MEDIA_SOURCE` renders blank/idle.
- `VIDEO` is an ordinary layout citizen: its box, size modifiers,
  `CONTENT_MODE`, `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, and style modifiers behave as for any view.

---

## 4. Events

The media event family reports a **controller's** playback state back to the
application. `A` = the **controller** node id (never a surface id).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags |
|---------|-------|----|----|----|-------|
| `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` | `0x0F` | controller id | playing (0/1) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` | `0x10` | controller id | seconds (f32) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_ENDED` | `0x11` | controller id | 0 | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` | `0x12` | controller id | volume (f32, 0..1) | 0 | — |
| `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` | `0x14` | controller id | seconds (f32) | 0 | — |

The full event table, encoding, and cadence live in
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#media).

### 4.1 Guards

- Media events flow **by virtue of the controller** — no `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit,
  mirroring `VALUE_CHANGED`.
- They flow **only when the application bound the matching control property on
  the controller**: `PLAYBACK_STATE` gates `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` and
  `MEDIA_ENDED`; `MEDIA_POSITION` gates `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` and
  `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED`; `MEDIA_VOLUME` gates `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED`. An
  unbound controller reports nothing (so a purely renderer-native playback stays
  silent).
- The gates are evaluated **on the controller**, not on the surface: binding a
  transport property on a surface has no effect.

### 4.2 Commands vs. reports (MUST)

`MEDIA_POSITION` / `MEDIA_VOLUME` are **commands**; `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` /
`MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` are **reports**. An application
MUST NOT bind a command property to the signal its matching report updates — that
echoes every report back as a command. Bind the command to a
**user-interaction-only** signal and route the report to a separate display
signal.

### 4.3 Renderer echo guard (MUST)

A renderer MUST NOT act on a command write that matches the value it last
**reported** (within an epsilon): the application is echoing the report back, not
interacting. A `MEDIA_POSITION` write within `0.25 s` of the last
`MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` must not seek; a `MEDIA_VOLUME` write within `0.01` of the
last `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` must not re-apply. The guard is **per controller**.

---

## 5. Structural swaps (the motivating contract)

The reason the controller exists. Consider a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` slot whose
candidates are two different **control layouts for the same track** — a compact
player bar and a wide now-playing sidebar (ordinary application views: buttons, a
seek slider, labels). Both write the same controller's transport signals:

```
VStack
  MEDIA_CONTROLLER (id 9)        ← stable: outside the slot
  SIZE_THAT_FITS (id 4)          ← the swapping slot
    candidate 0: PlayerBar       → controls controller 9
    candidate 1: NowPlayingBar   → controls controller 9
```

(For video the same shape holds with a `VIDEO` surface inside each candidate,
referencing the same controller.)

On a band crossing the application swaps the slot's child: the renderer
`DELETE_NODE`s the outgoing subtree and `CREATE_NODE`s the incoming one. What
MUST hold:

1. **Playback continues.** The renderer MUST NOT stop, restart, re-load, or
   re-seek the controller's playback because a view was destroyed/created. Its
   current position, play state, volume, mute, loop, and rate are preserved.
2. **The event target is stable.** Reports continue to carry the controller id
   (9), so the application's bindings never see a "moving target" across a swap.
3. **Zero opcodes for the controller.** The swap emits `TREE` deltas for the
   swapped views only; the controller emits nothing (nothing changed about it).
4. **Nothing is keyed by the swapped node.** The renderer MUST NOT key playback
   by any node other than the controller id. Playback is keyed **by controller
   id** — one playback per controller, for the life of the controller node.

A controller that is itself destroyed (its `DELETE_NODE`) releases its playback.
Creating a new controller starts a new playback.

---

## 6. Renderer obligations

- **One playback per controller.** A renderer MUST map a controller id to a
  single playback (a native media element / player) and reuse it for the
  controller's whole lifetime, regardless of how many views reference it or
  how often they are swapped.
- **Never restart on view change.** Creating, deleting, or reordering the views
  that reference a controller — including a `VIDEO` surface — is not a transport
  event (§5).
- **Video controls** follow the ordinary dual-mode rule: a `VIDEO` with no
  children presents renderer-native video controls; with children the children
  are the control UI. **Audio has neither a visual nor controls** — a renderer
  MUST NOT synthesize any audio UI, native or otherwise; the application's own
  views are the entire control surface (§1).
- **Playback is renderer output state, not application state.** The controller's
  authoritative transport values are the application's (written as commands and
  reported back as events). The renderer holds its playback — the media element,
  its position, its buffering — as a cache of its own output, exactly as a DOM
  `<audio>`/`<video>` element does. It MUST NOT invent transport state the
  application did not ask for, and it MUST NOT treat the media element's internal
  state as the application's model (that is what the reports are for).
- **Unknown component ids** (including a `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` from a newer spec
  revision) follow the standard rule: render blank, keep decoding.

---

## 7. Future / drafts

Not part of this version; listed so the ids can be allocated spec-first:

- `MEDIA_BUFFERING` (F32 0..1) + `MEDIA_BUFFERING_CHANGED` — readiness.
- Track selection (`MEDIA_AUDIO_TRACK`, `MEDIA_SUBTITLE_TRACK`) — video-ish, but
  the transport is shared.
- Picture-in-picture / fullscreen — currently renderer-owned chrome.
- Gapless / crossfade — an audio-only transport extension.
- `POSTER_SOURCE` (on a `VIDEO` surface) — a preview frame before playback.

   241	    private fun reconcileSnapshotFit(
   242	        slot: ViewSlot,
   243	        old: PathlandNode,
   244	        fresh: PathlandNode,
   245	        oldChildren: List<ViewSlot>,
   246	        newChildren: List<ViewSlot>,
   247	    ) {
   248	        val candidates = old.children.filterNot { isControllerNode(it) }
   249	        val selected = minOf(maxOf(fresh.fitSelection, 0), candidates.size - 1)
   250	        val keep = candidates[selected]
   251	        val keepSlot = keep.slot
   252	        val controllers = LinkedHashSet<PathlandNode>()
   253	        controllers.addAll(old.children.filter {
   254	            isControllerNode(it) && registeredMediaControllers.contains(it.mediaControllerRef)
   255	        })
   256	        controllers.addAll(fresh.children.filter {
   257	            isControllerNode(it) && registeredMediaControllers.contains(it.mediaControllerRef)
   258	        })
   259	        val dropOps = ArrayList<Runnable>()
   260	        for (child in old.children) {
   261	            if (child === keep) continue
   262	            if (isControllerNode(child) &&
   263	                registeredMediaControllers.contains(child.mediaControllerRef)
   264	            ) continue
   265	            val parentId = old.id
   266	            val childId = child.id
   267	            dropOps.add(Runnable {
   268	                sink.removeChild(parentId, childId)
   269	                sink.deleteNode(childId)
   270	            })
   271	        }
   272	        for (child in oldChildren) if (child !== keepSlot) destroySlotTree(child)
   273	        for (child in newChildren) destroySlotTree(child)
   274	        old.children.clear()
   275	        old.children.add(keep)
   276	        old.children.addAll(controllers)
   277	        fresh.children.clear()
   278	        fresh.children.add(keep)
   279	        fresh.children.addAll(controllers)
   280	        slot.children.clear()
   281	        if (keepSlot != null) slot.children.add(keepSlot)
   282	        fresh.id = old.id
   283	        if (dropOps.isNotEmpty()) {
   284	            sink.beginFrame()
   285	            for (op in dropOps) op.run()
   286	            sink.endFrame()
   287	        }
   288	        val ops = ArrayList<Runnable>()
   289	        reconcileNode(old, fresh, ops)
   290	        if (ops.isNotEmpty()) {
   291	            sink.beginFrame()
   292	            for (op in ops) op.run()
   293	            sink.endFrame()
   294	        }
   295	        slot.node = fresh
   296	        val parent = slot.nodeParent
   297	        if (parent != null) parent.children[slot.nodeIndex] = fresh else tree = fresh
   298	        linkSlots(fresh)
   299	        registerSlotBindings(slot)
   300	        collectSlotInputs(slot, null)
   301	        refreshNavigateHandler()
   302	        guardUniqueIds()
   303	        fireStructureReconciled()
   304	    }

+/**
+ * The music player demo root view — an Apple Music-style player authored purely
+ * with the Kotlin DSL, composed of the [PlayerMainArea] (library + floating
+ * player bar) and the wide-layout [NowPlayingSidebar].
+ *
+ * The root owns the per-session [MediaPlayerService] and scopes it through the
+ * environment; child views resolve the service instead of receiving its signals
+ * through their constructors.
+ */
+class MusicPlayerView @JvmOverloads constructor(
+    private val adUrl: String? = null,
+) : Component() {
+
+    companion object {
+        const val SIDEBAR_WIDTH = 280f
+        const val BAR_HEIGHT = 76f
+
+        // Gray-600: >= 4.5:1 on white, the sidebar, the selected row, and the player bar.
+        val SECONDARY_FG: Color = Color.rgb(0x4B, 0x55, 0x63)
+        val ACTIVE_ROW_BG: Color = Color.rgb(0xE8, 0xEF, 0xFF)
+        val ACTIVE_ROW_FG: Color = Color.rgb(0x1A, 0x3A, 0x8C)
+        val SIDEBAR_BG: Color = Color.rgb(0xF6, 0xF7, 0xFA)
+        val BAR_BORDER: Color = Color.rgb(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
+        val BAR_BG: Color = Color.argb(0xBF, 0xEB, 0xEB, 0xED)
+
+        /** A player with no sponsored slot (Java-compatible factory). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun make(): MusicPlayerView = MusicPlayerView()
+
+        /** A player with a sponsored slot proxying [adUrl] (Java-compatible factory). */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun make(adUrl: String?): MusicPlayerView = MusicPlayerView(adUrl)
+    }
+
+    private val service by lazy { MediaPlayerService() }
+
+    override fun body(): View {
+        val mediaPlayer = service
+
+        // One root fit slot selects the complete layout for the window width:
+        // narrow (no volume), medium (volume), wide (volume + now-playing sidebar).
+        // Keeping the bar's breakpoint at the root avoids a nested fit slot whose
+        // wide-only children could survive a parent candidate swap.
+        val narrowRow = HStack {
+            PlayerMainArea(showVolume = false)
+        }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
+
+        val mediumRow = HStack {
+            PlayerMainArea(showVolume = true)
+        }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
+
+        val wideRow = HStack {
+            PlayerMainArea(showVolume = true)
+            NowPlayingSidebar(adUrl).clipped()
+        }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
+
+        return VStack {
+            ViewThatFits(
+                Fit(narrowRow),
+                Fit(mediumRow, 700f),
+                Fit(wideRow, 1024f),
+            ).frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
+                .accessibilityRole(Roles.MAIN)
+        }.frame(width = Commands.Size.FILL, height = Commands.Size.FILL)
+            .environment(MediaPlayerService.KEY, mediaPlayer)
+            .windowMetadata {
+                title(computed { "Pathland · " + mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().title })
+                description(computed {
+                    mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().artist + " · " + mediaPlayer.currentTrack.get().album
+                })
+                locale("en")
+            }
+    }
+}
